title: Nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild black holes for the Einstein-massless Dirac system in spherical symmetry
summary: In this paper, we establish the nonlinear stability of the Schwarzschild exterior for the spherically symmetric Einstein-massless Dirac system. More precisely, we consider sufficiently small perturbations of Schwarzschild characteristic initial data and prove that the corresponding maximal development remains globally controlled in the exterior region (orbital stability), and converges, in a suitable teleological double-null gauge, to a Schwarzschild spacetime with a final mass (asymptotic stability). In particular, the maximal future development contains a complete future null infinity and a regular event horizon, with a nonempty black hole region in its interior. The main difficulties in the proof arise from the delicate coupling between the Dirac operator and the geometry, compared with the scalar wave counterpart, as well as from the failure of the Dirac stress-energy tensor to satisfy a positive energy condition. To overcome these difficulties, we rely on a bootstrap argument coupling the geometry and the Dirac field. Working in suitable teleological double-null gauges adapted to the asymptotic null boundaries, we establish weighted energy estimates combining integrated local energy decay, red-shift estimates near the event horizon, and an rp-estimates towards null infinity. A core ingredient is the use of suitable reweightings of the spinor components, which allow us to close these estimates despite the nonlinear coupling to the geometry.

title: Gauge-invariant non-universal scalar couplings in teleparallel gravity
summary: We develop a gauge-invariant teleparallel framework in which the universality of the gravitational coupling is relaxed for a scalar field, while the gravitational sector retains the form of the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity. The non-universal interaction is encoded in a scalar-sector tetrad whose coupling to the universal translational gauge potential is controlled by a field-dependent gravitational charge. A Stückelberg completion preserves local translational gauge invariance, and we derive the gravitational, scalar-field, and Stückelberg equations, together with the antisymmetric constraint and their consistency relations. As a first application, we investigate homogeneous and isotropic cosmology, where the Stückelberg constraint provides a first integral governing the evolution of the non-universal coupling. In the kination-dominated regime, the standard stiff-fluid behavior is recovered asymptotically, whereas in the potential-dominated regime, accelerated expansion requires additional conditions beyond potential domination. We identify compatible expanding solutions in which departures from universality are dynamically suppressed, including examples approaching power-law inflation or asymptotically de Sitter expansion. Including a universally coupled perfect fluid and a constant scalar potential, we obtain a late-time solution exhibiting a subdominant matter-like contribution to the background Friedmann equation and an asymptotic de Sitter limit. These results provide a gauge-theoretic realization of non-universal scalar couplings and highlight their potential implications for early- and late-time cosmology.

title: Reference-renormalized Jacobi primitives for finite-distance massive-particle deflection
comment: 19 pages, 1 figure. Under consideration in PRD
summary: We develop a reference-renormalized Jacobi-primitive Gauss-Bonnet formalism for finite-distance weak deflection of massive particles in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. The construction uses the fixed-energy Jacobi metric associated with timelike geodesics and treats the radial curvature primitive as a quantity defined only up to an additive constant. Instead of fixing this constant by requiring the primitive to vanish at a circular timelike orbit, we subtract a reference Jacobi geometry at the same conserved particle energy and impose endpoint normalization on the curvature-density discrepancy. This gives a circular-orbit-free primitive representation of the Gauss-Bonnet curvature contribution while preserving the operational finite-distance definition of the bending angle through local source and receiver directions. We prove that the reference-normalized and circular-orbit-normalized prescriptions agree whenever both are admissible, since their primitives differ only by a constant that cancels from the exact curvature strip integral. The method remains applicable when no admissible circular timelike orbit exists, when the orbit lies outside the Riemannian Jacobi domain, or when the natural no-lens comparison geometry is non-Euclidean. We demonstrate the formalism in three representative settings: Schwarzschild-like bumblebee, Kottler, and Janis-Newman-Winicour (JNW) spacetimes. The formalism therefore identifies circular-orbit anchoring as an auxiliary primitive gauge choice rather than a prerequisite for finite-distance Jacobi Gauss-Bonnet deflection.

title: Effective Optical Geometry and Holographic Phase Structure of a Magnetic AdS Black Hole
summary: We study circular null orbits, thermodynamic topology, and the holographic thermodynamic description of a four-dimensional magnetically charged AdS black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics. The background orbit structure is classified using Duan s phi-mapping construction and compared with the extraordinary electromagnetic characteristics. The latter defines an effective optical metric with an additional radial factor that modifies the orbit condition and introduces explicit dependence on the AdS radius. For four representative configurations, the local indices of the five isolated orbits are unchanged while their radii shift by up to 5.187 %. The background mass thresholds vary smoothly across sigma = 1/4 when the total mass is used, whereas the fixed-m0 parametrization is singular there. Regularity at the center requires sigma > 1 and m0 = 0. The thermodynamic analysis separates local stability indices from equilibrium coexistence: stable Gibbs-free-energy branches cross only in model-dependent parameter intervals. The boundary canonical ensemble exhibits critical behavior consistent with mean-field exponents, and the examined grand-canonical ensemble has a Hawking-Page crossing. In the mixed ensemble, the free-energy branches have a finite endpoint discontinuity, but the sampled competing states do not satisfy the full local-stability criterion

title: Constraints on a Long-Lived X17 Vector Boson with FASER
summary: The ATOMKI anomalies motivate the possibility of a new particle, the X17, with a mass of 17 MeV and weak couplings to nuclei and electrons. Such a particle may be produced at the LHC, travel 480 m in the far-forward direction, and decay to $e^+e^-$ in FASER. In this paper, previous FASER searches for dark photons and axion-like particles (ALPs) are combined and interpreted as searches for a candidate X17 particle, the protophobic vector boson. The searches use data collected from $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV in LHC Run 3 from 2022 for the dark photon search and from 2022-2023 for the ALP search. No excess events are found above the expected background, and the combined null results exclude a previously-unconstrained "low-coupling window" with electron coupling $6 \times 10^{-5} < ε_e < 1.2 \times 10^{-4}$. A "high-coupling window" remains.

title: On the Geometric Structure of Hyperbolic Clifford Bundles and Associated Spin Groups
summary: In this paper, we present the spinor structure associated with the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra of a real $n$-dimensional vector space $V$, which is denoted by $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$. Unlike the standard Clifford algebra, the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathcal{C}l(H_V)$ simultaneously accommodates both multiforms and multivectors in a single algebraic structure, making it the natural framework---known as the ``mother algebra''---for the study of superfields in theoretical physics and for generalizing the Clifford bundle formalism to hyperbolic structures arising in gravitational theories. The orthogonal groups and orthogonal transformations associated to the hyperbolic space $H_{V}$ are presented. The Clifford--Lipschitz group and the Pin and Spin groups associated with $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$ are defined. Then, the frame bundle and spinor structure associated to Hyperbolic Clifford algebra is derived.

title: Linear Response in the $\mathcal{PT}$-Broken Phase: Conductivity of Fermions with Complex Conjugate Masses
summary: We examine the linear response of the $\PT$-broken phase of a BRST invariant model whose fermion masses form the complex conjugate pair $m_{\pm}=N\pm iav$. It splits into two channels, kept apart by an exact $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, and one Euclidean correlator decides both. In the diagonal channel it oscillates in Euclidean time, so that channel admits no positive-norm realization: we exhibit a test function of negative norm and close every repair, the choice of boundary value among them. In the mixed channel the same correlator is completely monotone, which proves the spectral density positive; there we obtain the vacuum conductivity in closed form, with a real threshold at $ω=2N$, and positivity survives at finite temperature below a bound whose onset we give exactly. The longitudinal density of that channel is negative by the square of the mass splitting; an antisymmetric derivative removes it, and the resulting field-strength composite has a positive one-particle space and a causal commutator --- at the level of the two-point function only, since a four-point reflection form on the original composite comes out negative. The positive realization is therefore not a sector of the fermion model.

title: Correlated quantum criticality and topological magnetoelectric response in Bi2Se3
comment: 20 pages, 8 Figures, Submitted to npj Quantum Materials for consideration as a research article in the Special Collection \textit{Intertwined Orders in Quantum Materials--- In Memory of Daniel Khomskii}
summary: A defining feature of quantum materials is that multiple orders govern low-energy physics and are not independent. We study Bi$_2$Se$_3$ by combining DFT with a renormalized correlated honeycomb model in which frustrated magnetic order and helical topological surface states are coupled via one control parameter. The surface states map to a honeycomb Hubbard model with frustrated $J_1$--$J_2$ exchange. Exact diagonalization up to 20 sites shows the Néel structure factor and valence-bond-solid order parameter cross at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.22$, agreeing with QMC/DMRG, and a dynamical spin structure factor broadens near the crossover, as expected for a spinon continuum. Band inversion of the renormalized tight-binding model occurs on the same critical locus, producing jumps in the Chern number and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant mirrored by the skyrmion charge $Q$. This gives a microscopic link: $Q$ selects the axion angle and thus the topological magnetoelectric coupling. We distinguish axion coupling, independent of skyrmion helicity, from the helicity-dependent magnetoelectric multipole coupling, whose toroidal component scales as $\sinγ$ and vanishes for Néel-type textures. We derive the $Q$-topological magnetoelectric energy and estimate $\sim 10^{-20}\,\mathrm{J}$ per skyrmion per cycle for few-tesla fields. The cycle is thermodynamically bounded: constant-$θ$ cycles extract no net work, and efficiency is limited by axionic entropy change.

title: Nonexistence of Multiple Black Holes in Stationary Analytic Vacuum spacetimes
summary: We prove the nonexistence of non-rotating and degenerate horizon components in the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum spacetime. This result rules out the final case in the classification of stationary analytic black-hole spacetimes. Consequently, the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum black hole uniqueness conjecture is settled affirmatively in full.

title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
summary: The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date -- improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude -- and paves the way for precision measurements.

title: A hybrid quantum-classical lattice kinetic scheme with tensor-train feedback for incompressible flows
summary: Nonlinear lattice kinetic simulation requires each updated distribution to supply the velocity and gradients that determine the next step. In a quantum-classical solver, reading out the full distribution incurs work proportional to the lattice size. We construct a tensor-train (TT) interface that retains reusable classical cores at the physical amplitude scale for a full-relaxation lattice kinetic scheme. The cores supply nonlinear coefficients and prepare each quantum input. Energy-scaled propagation and coordinate recovery encode the updated distribution, and alternating least-squares reconstruction converts signed Hadamard-test overlaps into output cores by restoring a known normalization factor. The next step starts from accepted cores without replaying previous quantum evolution. Under positive, unit-sum reference coefficients, positive lower and finite upper density bounds, and Lipschitz equilibrium sensitivity, perturbation bounds relate local defects to feedback errors. Resource bounds account for classical operations, circuit execution, sampling, and verification. Classical diagnostics expose why distribution accuracy alone is insufficient: in 80-step feedback on a $16\times16$ grid, rank cap 4 nearly eliminates the vortex despite a final distribution error below $1\%$, whereas rank cap 12 gives relative velocity error $1.03\times10^{-3}$. Four-step binomial readout simulations show that tightening core sampling tolerance threefold raises the prescribed sufficient budget from $5.97\times10^{12}$ to $5.37\times10^{13}$ shots as the result approaches the fixed-rank, fixed-sweep exact-overlap trajectory. The interface therefore provides a way to connect quantum propagation to nonlinear feedback and to assess the separate demands of compression, velocity accuracy, and readout precision.

title: Meet biform singletons in your area! Topological actions for edge modes
summary: We present topological field theories propagating biform singleton fields as edge modes. In even spacetime dimensions $D=2p$, these are irreducible representations of the conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,2p)$ with two-column Young diagrams of height $p$. Their duality properties depend on the parity of $p$: They propagate chiral degrees of freedom for odd $p$, and exhibit electric--magnetic duality for even $p$. We are able to construct the topological actions by realising the hidden conformal symmetry inherent to singletons geometrically in terms of an auxiliary bulk $\text{AdS}_{2p+1}$ geometry. Using these as a starting point, we are able to apply a recently established covariant boundary reduction procedure to yield novel action formulations with manifest Lorentz covariance. We also show how, breaking manifest Lorentz covariance, we recover known formulations of biform singletons.

title: When do machine-learning potentials need a configuration-dependent kernel? Learning long-range interactions with Fourier neural operators
summary: Long-range interactions in machine-learning interatomic potentials are commonly treated by coupling learned sources through either a prescribed electrostatic kernel or a learned but configuration-independent one. Whether such a kernel suffices depends on the underlying screened interaction. We address this question by using Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn how latent source fields, built from the descriptors of a local backbone (here MACE), interact across the simulation cell. For a synthetic ionic system with tunable screening, a prescribed Coulomb kernel underestimates the long-wavelength charge fluctuations by 43% under strong screening, whereas the FNO reproduces them within 3% and recovers 95-99% of the variance of the residual left by the local backbone. A linear FNO, which learns a configuration-independent kernel, performs equally well in the homogeneous case. Under inhomogeneous screening, rearranging the remote medium modulates the coupling between distant ions, a dependence that no configuration-independent kernel can represent. Among the models tested, only the nonlinear FNO responds to this modulation, and its force errors are 27-41% lower than those of configuration-independent models. In first-principles benchmarks of liquid water, lithium lanthanum zirconate, and Au2/MgO(001), MACE-FNO is comparable to a prescribed-kernel model for the bulk systems and more accurate for the interface. It further captures the reversal of the Au2 wetting preference induced by remote Al dopants, with deviations below 5 meV per cell from density functional theory. These results indicate that a configuration-dependent kernel, as learned by FNOs, becomes necessary once the screening medium varies, even though the energy remains quadratic in the charges for a fixed medium.

title: Bouncing and QNM convergence in Kerr
summary: We show that the convergence region of the QNM representation of the retarded Green's function of the Kerr spacetime is set by complex-time bouncing singularities, as in our previous work for the Schwarzschild case. The main difference between Kerr and Schwarzschild is that there are two distinct QNM families, prolate and oblate, which have different convergence regions. We provide explicit analytical formulae for the bounce radii and corresponding convergence regions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates. We also provide an analysis of convergence in the Reissner-Nordström spacetime.

title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
summary: We measure the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb$^{-1}$ of BaBar initial-state radiation data. The result is obtained from the $π^+π^-/μ^+μ^-$ ratio, reducing systematic uncertainties that are in common. Unlike the previous 2009 BaBar analysis, the pion and muon contributions are separated statistically through their angular distributions. The compatibility with the previous BaBar result is quantified including statistical and systematic correlations. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results as a function of energy and in terms of its hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly. The leading-order HVP contribution of the two-pion channel in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV is $a_μ^{ππ}=525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$ for the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements, respectively.

title: Eigenstates on $O^\ast$-algebras with an application to ladder operators
summary: Following some recent results, we consider here a particular class of states on a $O^\ast$-algebra $\M$ which we call {\em eigenstates of an element} $A\in\M$, and we deduce some of their properties. Then, we apply our definition to a family of ladder elements, i.e. elements of $\M$ obeying certain algebraic (commutation) relations which are physically motivated, and we discuss several results for these states

title: Worldsheet functional RG and the $α'$-tower
summary: We apply the functional renormalization group to the worldsheet theory of the bosonic string. Imposing the Weyl anomaly cancellation as a condition on the local renormalization group flow, we derive flow equations for the background couplings and the corresponding effective spacetime equations of motion, first in a two-derivative truncation, on a general curved background. We then consider a truncation to all orders in $α'$, which captures only a subset of the possible tensor structures but is analytically tractable, in analogy with $f(R)$-like approximations. Within this truncation, we obtain Tseytlin's spacetime effective action, and we use it to study solutions to all orders in $α'$, including black holes. Our results show that the functional renormalization group can be implemented on the string worldsheet and provide a framework to access the strong-curvature regime. As a longer-term goal, this may allow one to test the scenario of effective asymptotic safety in string theory, in which an approximately scale-invariant regime lies between the low-energy effective field theory and a stringy completion.

title: Restricted triangular ice beyond the solvable manifolds: chiral ice and the critical region of dominant chiral vertices
summary: We study two restrictions of Baxter's symmetric twenty-vertex model on the triangular lattice, in which the three classes of vertices allowed by the ice rule carry the weights $a$, $b$ and $c$: chiral ice, in which only the twelve chiral vertices are allowed, and the model that excludes only the two alternating vertices. We show that neither model belongs to any of the known exactly solvable families of the twenty-vertex model, and we characterise chiral ice as the ice model in which every vertex has exactly one through line, a property that imposes a parity constraint along every closed lattice line. We compute the residual entropies of both models with transfer matrices on cylinders of up to twelve vertices in circumference, extrapolated with the finite-size correction predicted by conformal invariance, which we adapt to the triangular geometry and verify at two exactly solved points. The number of upward arrows crossing the cylinder is conserved, and the cost of changing it shows that both models are critical, with the long-distance behaviour of a free massless field. Chiral ice is the extreme point of a region of the phase diagram in which ordering had been suggested; along two paths through that region we find the same critical behaviour at every point, with no feature at the proposed boundary of the region. Along Baxter's exactly solved curve we obtain the corresponding exponents in closed form.

title: Electrically charged black holes with electroweak hair
summary: We construct electrically charged black holes in Einstein's gravity coupled to the bosonic sector of the electroweak theory, focusing on static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat solutions, with the weak mixing angle fixed to its Standard Model value. Horizon regularity imposes a resonance condition relating the charged-vector frequency to the electromagnetic potential at the horizon, corresponding to the threshold of charged superradiance. A perturbative analysis further shows that nonextremal Reissner-Nordström black holes do not support regular, exponentially localized, spherically symmetric electroweak clouds satisfying such condition. Thus, the hairy solutions cannot emerge via a bifurcation from this electrovacuum family. Moreover, our numerical investigation reveals two apparently disconnected families of bosonic stars. Within the explored parameter space, the hairy black holes are connected to the strongly gravitating one.

title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
summary: We report precise results for the $e^+e^-\to π^+π^-(γ)$ cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$ prediction. Using the full 460 fb$^{-1}$ of on- and off-$Υ(4S)$ data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of $π^+π^-$ to $μ^+μ^-$ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV are $525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$, respectively.

title: An Excursion into Grassmannian Spectra
summary: We revisit the classical spectral problem for the Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians. After reviewing the standard approach based on non-commutative harmonic analysis, we develop two complementary methods originating from the quantization of the corresponding one-dimensional sigma model, both with and without a magnetic monopole field. The first is based on $\mathbf{SU}(n)$-equivariant first-order GLSM formulation and gives explicit eigenfunctions in terms of projectors and Plücker coordinates. The second uses a spin-chain realization of free particles on manifolds and describes the space of square-integrable functions, or sections in the magnetic case, through limiting tensor products of long rectangular $\mathbf{SU}(n)$ representations. Together, these approaches provide a more explicit picture of the spectral geometry of Grassmannians and clarify the relation between harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and Laplacian spectra.

title: A New Holographic Duality for Conformal Mass Deformations
summary: We construct a space-dependent conformal mass deformation of ABJM on the half-space $z>0$ and show that the vacua of this theory are dual to a large class of half-BPS bubbling solutions of the form $AdS_3\times S^3\times S^3\timesΣ$, with superalgebra $D(2,1|γ)^{\oplus2}$, parametrized by $γ<0$. The conformal symmetry of a plane is preserved provided that the mass deformation scales as $m(z)=\frac{c}{z}$. We give the first field-theory explanation of the exceptional superalgebra parameter $γ$ in M2-brane field theory in terms of the coefficient of the inverse-distance mass deformation of ABJM: $γ=\frac{1-2c}{1+2c}$. We demonstrate this using the methods of Polchinski and Strassler, which we first apply to the Janus interfaces of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills and ABJM to relate localized mass sources to scalar matching conditions.

title: Current-Confined Formation of a Buried Ge/Si Free Surface for Defect Filtering
summary: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. STEM reveals an approximately 15 Ang separation, while EDX shows localized interfacial oxygen enrichment. After soft annealing, geometric phase analysis and plan-view TEM show a modified strain-relaxation pathway and strongly suppressed threading-dislocation emergence. Raman spectroscopy indicates a reduction in residual tensile strain from approximately 0.10 % to 0.05 %, whereas spreading resistance profiling confirms preservation of the Ge carrier profile. Current-confined electrochemistry therefore provides a controllable post-epitaxial route for buried-interface decoupling, defect filtering, and strain control in lattice-mismatched semiconductor heterostructures.

title: Multi-domain spectral method for Kerr spacetimes: a hyperboloidal Teukolsky $m$-mode solver for self-force computations
summary: We solve the frequency-domain, $m$-mode Teukolsky equation for the spin-weight $s=-2$ Weyl scalar $ψ_4$ sourced by a point mass on a circular, equatorial orbit around a Kerr black hole. The equation is posed on hyperboloidal slices that reach the event horizon and future null infinity, so that the physical (retarded) solution is selected by regularity alone, without imposing radiation conditions. The particle is treated with the $m$-mode puncture/effective-source scheme, and the resulting two-dimensional elliptic problem is solved with a four-domain pseudo-spectral method in which the equatorial symmetry is broken and handled by an even/odd decomposition of the field. We test the method for orbital radius $r_0=10M$ and spins up to $|a|/M=0.9$, covering prograde and retrograde orbits. The energy fluxes to infinity agree with independent Black Hole Perturbation Toolkit results to $\sim10^{-7}$ for the dominant modes and to better than $2\times10^{-5}$ for all modes up to $m=20$ at moderate resolutions. The static $m=0$ mode requires no special treatment.

title: Search for heavy neutral leptons in top quark decays with same-sign, same-flavor dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/B2G-24-023 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for a Majorana-type heavy neutral lepton (HNL) produced in top quark decays is reported. The search is based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, collected during 2016$-$2018 with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. In the type-I seesaw model, a Majorana HNL can mediate lepton-number-violating top quark decays. The search targets top quark pair production events in which one top quark decays into a bottom quark and a W boson, which subsequently decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and an HNL. The Majorana HNL then decays into a W boson and a charged lepton with the same sign and flavor as the one produced with the HNL. The experimental signature features a same-sign, same-flavor lepton pair and jets. The HNL masses between 20 and 100 GeV are probed. The data agree with the standard model background prediction. Observed (expected) upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the branching fraction of the top quark decay into an HNL, a charged lepton, and a bottom quark, varying between [1.1 (0.71)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ and [4.8 (3.0)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dielectron channel, and between [3.7 (3.4)] $\times$10$^{-6}$ and [2.4 (1.3)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dimuon channel.

title: Lorentz-Invariant Measure for Path Integrals in the Future Cone
summary:
We construct a measure on continuous paths in the future cone of two-dimensional space that is invariant under the orthochronous Lorentz group and quasi-invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group.
  We use the proposed measure to obtain the fundamental solution of the heat equation. The result agrees with the expression obtained by other methods.

title: Chaos on the mass shell
summary: We study particle production in high-energy states for theories given by an RG flow between an asymptotically free or conformal theory in the UV and a massive theory in the IR. Using the framework of detector matching, we argue that distributions of produced particles satisfy universal evolution equations with energy, determined by the spectrum of light-ray operators of the UV theory. In particular, we interpret the UV Chew-Frautschi plot as a wave equation for particle densities on the mass shell, evolving with energy. (When the UV theory is a CFT, this wave equation is the same one that controls the spread of chaos in hyperbolic space at a particular temperature.) We test these ideas for integrable flows in 2d CFTs, finding an independent derivation of the evolution equations in terms of the thermodynamics of a Feynman gas. We also discuss consequences for 4d gauge theories, including the presence of a BFKL contrail produced by an outgoing wave of hadron number density.

title: Agentic inverse design of spatially programmed materials
summary: Spatially programmed functional materials, from functionally graded alloys and metamaterials to quantum superlattices, use their spatial structure to tailor physical properties. However, translating a desired spatial structure into a practical fabrication recipe remains challenging due to the complex relationship between processing conditions and resulting material structures. Here we show that a large language model (LLM) agent can inverse-design such fabrication recipes by using a physics-based simulator of ion-matter interactions as a tool. Given an arbitrary depth profile of implanted ions or vacancies, the agent selects the ion species, energies, incident angles, and target material layers; writes, runs, and interprets simulations; and iteratively refines the recipe until the simulated profile matches the target, with minimal human input. Our work demonstrates physics-guided agentic inverse design as a practical approach to making the spatial structure of materials a programmable variable, opening new opportunities to explore emergent physical phenomena and functional phases of matter.

title: Kerr metric perturbations for second-order self-force theory
summary: We present a calculation of the first-order metric perturbation arising from a point mass moving on a circular, equatorial orbit in Kerr spacetime. The metric perturbation is specifically aimed at meeting the requirements of second-order self-force theory: it is highly accurate; incorporates all contributions, including those associated with perturbations to the black hole's mass and angular momentum; is in Lorenz gauge near the worldline and in (near) Bondi--Sachs gauge at large radius; and can be efficiently evaluated across the entire exterior spacetime. The Lorenz gauge gives a well-understood singular structure at the particle, while the (near) Bondi--Sachs gauge ensures the asymptotic fall-off needed for an asymptotically flat second-order source. Our formalism reconstructs the metric from separable Teukolsky-type equations, decomposed into spin-weighted spheroidal harmonic modes and solved spectrally on hyperboloidal slices. The resulting $(\ell,m)$-mode sums converge rapidly across most of the domain, but slowly near the point mass; we overcome this with a novel use of a puncture to extract accurate $m$-mode data, yielding output accurate to $\sim 10^{-10}$ per $m$-mode and suitable for use at second order. Our metric-perturbation results cover a range of Kerr spins $-0.9 \le a/M \le 0.9$ and orbital radii out to $50M$. In addition to its immediate application in second-order self-force calculations, our results can also be used as input to other calculations involving Kerr metric perturbations, including studies of environmental effects and quasinormal modes.

authors: Paul Swallow for the ANUBIS Collaboration
title: Projected sensitivity of the \anubis detector to photophobic and fermion-coupled axion-like particles
summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are a common benchmark for experiments at the lifetime frontier, as their suppressed couplings to Standard Model particles can render them long-lived on detector scales. This article presents the projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to two scenarios: a photophobic ALP model and a modified version of the flavour-diagonal, fermion-coupled ALP benchmark of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative that introduces an additional $h\to Za$ decay. For the photophobic case, the ANUBIS detector will reach a peak sensitivity of $σ_{Wa}\cdot Br(a\rightarrow gg)=6.2\times10^{-4}$~pb at $cτ=1.95$ m for an ALP mass of $10$ GeV. This will improve on the current exclusion limits from the ATLAS experiment by two orders of magnitude and extend the $cτ$ coverage by three orders of magnitude. For the fermion-coupled case with a dimension-seven Higgs--ALP interaction, the peak sensitivity to the fermion coupling is $C_{a^Φ}=4.4\times10^{-8}$, reached for ALP masses between $16$ and $23$ GeV. Overall, the ANUBIS detector is shown to provide unique coverage of the parameter space of both models, in regions that can be probed neither by the main LHC experiments nor by forward detectors at the HL-LHC.

title: An exact unstable mode of self-similar Yang--Mills solutionsin 5+1 dimensions
summary: Self-similar solutions play an important role in the formation of singularities in the Yang--Mills equations. In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $λ=5$. We explain this remarkable spectral property by an elementary construction of the corresponding eigenfunction in terms of the profile.

title: Inner Product of Closed Universe from Gravitational Path-integral
summary: We construct the Hilbert space of a closed universe of fixed topology in anti-de Sitter (AdS) and de Sitter (dS) Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity from the gravitational path integral. Quantizing gravity involves several subtleties, including the choice of lapse contour, path-integral measure, operator ordering, global structure of the gauge group, the implementation of gravitational constraints and the gauge symmetries at initial and final timeslices. We develop a formalism that addresses these issues and determines the inner product of physical states, providing a framework to assign probabilities to cosmological wavefunctions. For a fixed topology and a lapse contour, we compute the inner product exactly and obtain the corresponding resolution of the identity in JT gravity. We demonstrate that the co-invariant and invariant Hilbert spaces in refined algebraic quantization arise from particular gauge fixing at the initial and final timeslices. In particular, the formalism provides precise meaning for a gravitational wavefunction with fixed geometric data as a co-invariant state, including its integral measure. These constructions can be formulated within the Hamiltonian BFV-BRST formalism. We also discuss the global structure of the Hilbert space, which differs from that of BF theory and depends on the prescription adopted near the big bang/crunch. Our results imply that the cylinder geometry captures the gravitational inner product for all perturbative states, including the Hartle-Hawking no-boundary state.

title: Thermal Phase Transition of Three Dimensional Orthogonal Metals
summary: Orthogonal metals provide a paradigmatic example of strongly entangled metallic states whose transport and thermodynamic properties resemble those of conventional Fermi liquids, while their single-electron excitations remain fundamentally distinct. Despite considerable interest in their unusual ground-state properties, orthogonal metals in three spatial dimensions and their finite-temperature behavior remain relatively unexplored. Here, we investigate a three-dimensional orthogonal metal and characterize the thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures associated with its finite-temperature phase transition. Starting from a simple model of fermions coupled to spin degrees of freedom, we perturbatively demonstrate that the thermal transition known to occur in the purely bosonic limit persists in the presence of coupling to a gapless Fermi surface. We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes. In particular, we calculate the evolution of the physical-electron spectral function and identify characteristic signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find a pronounced contrast in low-energy spectral weight between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes without requiring conventional symmetry-breaking order. Our results establish finite-temperature orthogonal-metal physics as a possible mechanism for pseudogap-like behavior in three-dimensional and quasi-two-dimensional layered materials with non-negligible interlayer hopping, which may be applied to the recent experiments in $\mathrm{Sr_2 VO_3 Fe As}$.

title: Quasi-Normal Modes of Covariant Loop Quantum Black Holes
summary: We investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) and time-domain response of a massless, minimally coupled test scalar field on static, spherically symmetric covariant loop quantum black hole (cLQBH) backgrounds. Focusing on a phenomenological, Gaussian-localized holonomy profile, we obtain a localized deformation of the scalar effective potential containing both positive and negative parts. This provides a geometric realization of the bump effect, with the potential deformation and tortoise-coordinate mapping determined consistently by the same background. We characterize the deformation by its location, amplitude, and width, and study its effects using frequency-domain shooting and time-domain evolution, supplemented by matrix-pencil mode extraction and waveform reconstruction. The QNM spectrum exhibits spiral trajectories as the bump location varies, enhanced sensitivity of the overtones, and mode overtaking, whereby the branch continued from the first Schwarzschild overtone becomes longer-lived than the continued fundamental branch. Despite substantial spectral changes, the early response can remain close to its Schwarzschild counterpart, with more pronounced differences emerging later. To quantify this behavior, we introduce a local waveform-deviation time and compare it with a relative-amplitude faintness time, thereby defining an operational observation window. The deviation time depends nonmonotonically on the bump location, and suitable parameter choices allow appreciable departures to emerge before the adopted faintness threshold is reached. These results connect localized holonomy corrections with spectral sensitivity and waveform evolution, providing a basis for future gravitational-perturbation studies and assessments of gravitational-wave detectability.

title: BGRem: A background noise remover for astronomical images based on a diffusion model
comment: Accepted version in A&A before any editorial changes
summary:
Context: Astronomical imaging aims to maximize signal capture while minimizing noise. Enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio directly on detectors is difficult and expensive, leading to extensive research in advanced post-processing techniques.
  Aims: Removing background noise from images is a valuable pre-processing step catalog-building tasks. We introduce BGRem, a machine learning (ML) based tool to remove background noise from astronomical images.
  Methods: BGRem uses a diffusion-based model with an attention U-Net as backbone, trained on simulated images for optical and gamma (γ)-ray data from the MeerLICHT and Fermi-LAT telescopes. In a supervised manner, BGRem learns to denoise astronomical images over several diffusion steps.
  Results: BGRem performance was compared with a widely used tool for cataloging astronomical sources, SourceExtractor (SExtractor). It was shown that the amount of true positive sources using SExtractor increased by about 7% for MeerLICHT data when BGRem was used as a pre-processing step. We also show the generalizability of BGRem by testing it with optical images from different telescopes and also on simulated γ-ray data representative of the Fermi-LAT telescope. We show that in both cases, BGRem improves the source detection efficiency.
  Conclusions: BGRem can improve the accuracy in source detection of traditional pixel-based methods by removing complex background noise. Using zero-shot approach, BGRem can generalize well to a wide range of optical images. The successful application of BGRem to simulated γ-ray images, alongside optical data, demonstrates its adaptability to distinct noise characteristics and observational domains. This cross-wavelength performance highlights its potential as a general-purpose background removal framework for multi-wavelength astronomical surveys.

title: Multiplicity and parity in Hirota's $N$-soliton conditions: the bilinear families $L\,(D_x^{3}+Λ)^{2n+1}$
summary: Hirota's three-soliton condition is the standard test for the integrability of a bilinear equation $P(D)f\cdot f=0$, and the folklore implication ``three-soliton condition $\Rightarrow$ $N$-soliton solutions for all $N$'' underlies the classifications of Hietarinta. We study this implication in two directions. The first is the family $L\,(D_x^3+Λ)^{2n+1}f\cdot f=0$ with $L$, $Λ$ linear forms in the Hirota operators, which for $n=0$ contains the Korteweg--de Vries, Ito and Boiti--Leon--Manna--Pempinelli equations and for $L=D_x$ is the family of Gürses and Pekcan. On the principal component of the dispersion variety the $N$-soliton condition reduces to a sign sum of two bialternants; counting odd exponents shows that for $n=0$ the class is Hirota integrable and that for $n\ge1$ the three-soliton condition holds for every $L$, and an explicit formula for the four-soliton residual proves the Gürses--Pekcan conjecture that the four-soliton condition fails for every $n\ge1$. The formula yields sum-of-squares certificates excluding four-soliton solutions at every real configuration for the Gürses--Pekcan and Ito equations, classifies the real members of the class, and determines maximal numbers of nondegenerate solitons: exactly four or five for $n=1$ according as $L$ lies in the span of $D_x,Λ$ or not, five for $n=2$ and $L=D_x$, and finite for every $n\ge1$ and every $L$. The second direction is a reformulation of the implication for a single non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one, which we prove, with complete classifications, for all graph-type dispersions $L(q(D)+D_t)$, for every irreducible even quadric component in any dimension and with an arbitrary cofactor, for parabolic components, for the dispersions $F(\ell)+Q$ containing the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili surface, and, with a prescribed one-parameter phase family, for the cubic graph.

title: A Sojourn Through $c=1$ String Theory
summary: We revisit the $S$-matrix, the thermal $S$-matrix and the thermal free energy of $c=1$ string theory from the worldsheet perspective. By numerically integrating Virasoro conformal blocks with DOZZ structure constants, we compute the scattering amplitudes and thermal amplitudes up to 6-point at tree level and up to 3-point at one loop, in addition to the genus two thermal free energy. All results are in agreement with the predicted answers from the $c=1$ matrix model.

title: Collective Modes of Fractional States Beyond Landau Levels
summary: Collective modes provide a powerful probe into the properties and stability of topologically ordered and strongly interacting phases of matter, such as fractional quantum Hall states. Yet, the description of fractional-state excitations away from the Landau-level limit remains a formidable challenge. We develop a framework for describing collective excitations in the strong-coupling regime of coupled-wire constructions and show that they emerge as solitons and breathers of effective sine-Gordon theories. This approach provides a systematic route to studying collective modes in a broad class of fractional states. Applied to a coupled-wire construction of the fractional quantum Hall effect, the framework captures key features of the magnetoroton branch. It naturally extends to fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating that magnetoroton-like collective modes persist well beyond the Landau-level limit. We find that the magnetoroton gap increases as the Fubini-Study metric approaches the ideal (trace-condition) limit, highlighting the important role of quantum geometry in the stability of fractionalized phases and their collective excitations. The same trend favors the stability of the long-wavelength quadrupolar mode associated with the chiral graviton. Together, these results identify a distinct interplay between fractionalization and quantum geometry, and provide an analytical framework for studies of collective excitations in fractional topological matter.

title: Noisy pipelines II: Non-parametric Noise Inference for LISA
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to observe gravitational-wave signals from massive black hole binaries, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and more. Despite the significant scientific potential, accurately extracting these signals from the data will only be possible if LISA's instrumental noise is understood: poor noise modelling will result in lost signals, biased parameter estimates, and incorrect astrophysical insights. Modelling LISA's instrumental noise is more challenging than its ground-based counterpart since the data is highly correlated, meaning that the noise covariance matrix can no longer be assumed diagonal in frequency and in the different data streams. In this work, we present an initial approach to perform non-parametric noise inference for LISA that requires no prior knowledge of the LISA observatory. By fitting the full noise covariance matrix with a combination of splines and inverse Lorentzians, we show that our model can estimate the power and cross spectral densities for LISA from 7 days of simulated noise-only data. We find that the median estimate from our non-parametric model whitens the data according to the expected unit normal distribution. We envision that our non-parametric model can be used as part of the global fit, as well as in combination with modelled approaches to identify, quantify, and constrain the frequency dependence of unknown noise artifacts.

title: The First Deep Learning all-sky List of Fermi-LAT Gamma-ray Sources
summary:
Aims: We develop a deep-learning-based pipeline to construct a list of γ-ray sources and to quantitatively assess the impact of background uncertainties on source detection and characterization. This work extends and enhances the existing AutoSource-ID algorithm, previously adopted on optical observations, for applications on γ-ray data.
  Methods: Source detection was performed through image segmentation using a U-Net architecture, while dedicated deep neural networks (DNNs) were employed for source localization, flux estimation, and the classification of detected sources as either genuine or spurious. The training data were generated from Monte Carlo simulations based on 10 years of Fermi-LAT observations.
  Results: We present the first Fermi-LAT γ-ray all-sky source list derived using a deep-learning-based method (1FDL), containing more than 3800 sources with estimated positions, fluxes, and probability scores that quantify the likelihood of each detection being genuine or spurious. We further evaluated the robustness of the pipeline against variations in the interstellar emission model (IEM) and compared the resulting source list with the 4FGL-DR2 catalog.
  Conclusion: We find that the our deep-learning-based approach achieves performance comparable to, or better than, the likelihood-based methods employed in the standard Fermi-LAT catalog pipeline when tested against changes in the IEM. The 1FDL source list is broadly consistent with the Fermi-LAT 4FGL-DR2 catalog obtained over the same 10-year observational period, including a few new sources confirmed in the recent Fermi-LAT 16-year source list (FL16Y). These results demonstrate the potential of DNN methods for the detection and characterization of γ-ray sources and provide a foundation for their application in future high-energy astrophysical analyses.

title: High-order compact ALE gas-kinetic scheme on three-dimensional unstructured meshes
summary: In this paper, a compact high-order gas-kinetic scheme (HGKS) is developed for compressible arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) computations on three-dimensional unstructured meshes. To achieve high-order spatial accuracy, a large number of matrix inversions are required for spatial reconstruction. In ALE computations, the mesh moves and the geometric information must be recalculated at each time step, which reduces computational efficiency. To improve efficiency, a memory-reduction reconstruction strategy is employed to construct a quadratic polynomial on unstructured meshes. By differentiating the candidate polynomial, the quadratic terms are obtained by the least-squares method using the average gradient values of the cell itself and its neighboring cells. The linear terms of the polynomial are also determined by the least-squares method. On three-dimensional unstructured meshes, a $3\times3$ coefficient matrix must be stored, and four least-squares procedures are required to construct a quadratic polynomial. To suppress numerical oscillations in flows with discontinuities, generalized essentially non-oscillatory (GENO) reconstruction and a gradient compression factor are adopted. To accelerate the computation, a multi-GPU accelerated code is implemented using Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) and Message Passing Interface (MPI). The current scheme is fully explicit, and the acceleration framework can be developed based on cell-level parallelism. Numerical examples are presented to evaluate the accuracy and robustness of the scheme, including flows with strong discontinuities, pitching wings, and helicopter rotors. Numerical results confirm the excellent performance of the compact ALE scheme on unstructured meshes.

title: Compact holography via polarized IKKT
summary: The polarized IKKT matrix model is a $U(N)$ supersymmetric matrix integral proposed to be dual to an $N$ D-instanton sector of Euclidean type IIB string theory. We show a direct path from matrix model saddles to supergravity saddles: matrix model resolvent $\to$ holomorphic function $\to$ 2D Coulomb potential $\to$ 4D Coulomb potential $\to$ supergravity fields, where the last step was previously described. Here, the 2D electrostatics picture is an exact finite $N$ reformulation of a localization deformation of the matrix model that gives a constrained gas of dipoles in a background field. We show a matching between supergravity and matrix model on-shell actions and protected observables for all saddles. We show that the supergravity saddles have a compact and non-singular metric in string frame with the Einstein frame asymptotic region replaced by a pointlike D-instanton source. We provide evidence that the physics of particular gravity saddles can be obtained through restricting the domain of the matrix model integral to a basin associated with the corresponding matrix model saddle. We describe certain large $N$ decoupling limits where families of the saddles decouple from the rest to give the gravity duals of certain higher-dimensional field theories.

title: Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, Yb$_y$Co$_3$G$e_{3-x}$Sn$_x$
summary: Strong electron correlations and topology offer complementary routes to controlling electrical conduction, as correlations can make electrons heavy (e.g. Kondo lattices) whereas topology can make them behave as massless particles (e.g. Dirac or Weyl systems), and having both in one material is rare. In Kondo lattice systems, Kondo hybridization between localized 4$f$ and conduction electrons strongly enhances the quasiparticle mass, where in Weyl-Kondo systems these Kondo-renormalized bands form Weyl states, and simultaneous signs of both Kondo and Weyl states in one material have not been observed in transport. Here we report signs of both in the kagome metal \ce{Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x} by combining magnetotransport, heat capacity, magnetization, angle-resolved and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, and DFT+U calculations to reveal Yb-dependent Kondo scattering developing into lattice coherence, with extrapolated Sommerfeld coefficient of approximately 2 ~Jmol$_{\mathrm{Yb}}^{-1}$K$^{-2}$. Transverse magnetoresistance (MR) follows single-ion Kondo scaling, whereas longitudinal transport contains an additional negative response proportional to B$^2$ and remains unsaturated up to 32 T, consistent with a chiral anomaly. These findings support a picture of Kondo and Weyl-like conduction arising from distinct electronic states without external Fermi-level tuning, suggesting a possible route to combining correlated and topological functionality in a bulk material.

title: Binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
summary: We study fully non-linear binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity with a linear Gauss-Bonnet coupling function. In the absence of a well-developed initial data solver for EsGB gravity, we demonstrate that the conventional workaround solution for massless scalar fields results in confined junk radiation that contaminates late-time dynamics in the massive theory. We propose a solution to this problem by suitably modifying the equations of motion at the early stages of the simulation to tame such junk radiation, thereby allowing us to study the dynamics of the scalar field during the process of a black hole merger. This is followed by a preliminary analysis of the frequency content in the ringdown of the scalar and tensor modes. In particular, the quadrupole scalar mode exhibits a rich ringdown structure: while it is dominated by the spin-2 ``contamination'' frequency in the early stages, its late time morphology becomes primarily determined by the scalar mass frequency.

title: Electroweak Constraints on Nuclear Neutron Distributions and the Low-Energy Weak Mixing Angle
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures. Supplemental material will be included in the published version. Comments are welcome
summary: Coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) offers a low-energy probe of the weak mixing angle, $\sin^2θ_W$, and possible new physics in the neutrino sector. Its reliable interpretation, however, requires independent constraints on the neutron distributions of the target nuclei. We exploit correlations across nuclei within an extended Skyrme energy-density-functional framework to propagate constraints from the CREX and PREX-II parity-violating electron-scattering (PVES) measurements to CE$ν$NS targets. This yields neutron form factors and radii, with relative radius uncertainties below $1\%$. Using these inferred neutron form factors, we jointly analyze the COHERENT CsI, Ge, and Ar data and obtain $\sin^2θ_W=0.231^{+0.016}_{-0.015}$, consistent with the Standard Model prediction. These results provide the first electroweak-experimentally constrained benchmarks for nuclear-structure studies, neutrino-sector electroweak tests, and CE$ν$NS signal predictions in dark-matter detectors.

title: Rasterization-based discontinuous integration on the GPU
summary: In this paper, we propose a method based on rasterization in computer graphics for the integration of discontinuous functions accurately and efficiently on the GPU. The proposed method takes advantage of the massively parallel architecture of GPUs via a modified graphics pipeline, where discontinuities are encoded through geometric primitives and processed in the rasterization stage, and multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) is used to improve integration accuracy across subdomain interfaces. We present both hardware- and software-based pipelines and compare their performance in terms of accuracy as well as computational effort on modern GPU hardware with adaptive quadrature on the CPU. For the tested hardware, at approximately comparable median relative error, the hardware pipeline is up to around $100\text{x}$ faster than adaptive quadrature, while the single- and double-precision software pipelines achieve up to $840\text{x}$ and $1200\text{x}$ speedups compared to their adaptive quadrature counterparts. We use the finite cell method as model problem, where cutcells represent discontinuous integrands at the interface of the physical and fictitious domains and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method using numerical benchmarks. The end-to-end finite cell solution runtime is reduced by a factor of $8.3$ to $9.5$ in the single-precision pipeline and by a factor of $62$ to $72$ in the double-precision pipeline at the prescribed integration settings. Therefore, results indicate that the rasterization-based integration method is a promising alternative for the accurate and efficient integration of discontinuous functions in demanding applications on the GPU.

title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
summary: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.

title: The Inverse Mean First-Passage Time Problem
summary: We consider the mean first-passage time $τ(x)$ for an overdamped particle in a one-dimensional potential landscape, and address the problem inverse to the textbook one: Given $τ(x)$ as a function of starting distance, we look for a potential that realizes it. We derive the conditions on $τ(x)$ under which such a potential exists. We show that while the power-law dependences $τ(x)\sim x^α$ with $α\leq 2$ may be realized by monotonic potentials, any realizable $τ(x)$ with superquadratic growth requires potential wells arbitrarily far from the target; $α= 2$ separates sliding from trapping-dominated motion regimes.

title: Multimessenger astrophysics drives the case for an Australian Gravitational-Wave observatory
comment: 10 pages, 9 figures, submitted to Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia, comments welcome
summary: The next generation of an international network of gravitational-wave observatories is now in the advanced planning stages. With Australia's substantial history of contributions in this field, its history of scientific mega-projects like the Square Kilometer Array, and its unique geographic location and conditions, it is ideally placed to host an observatory in the global network. It has already been demonstrated that a gravitational wave detector in Australia plays an important role in minimizing the sky localization uncertainty of gravitational wave events. We study a particular science case for an Australian observatory, focusing on its potential contributions to multimessenger astronomy. We demonstrate that an observatory in Australia can enable the detection of up to eight multimessenger gravitational-wave plus kilonova events per year, with localisations better than $1-10°^2$ in both second- and third-generation networks. We show that, in a global network of XG observatories, an Australian observatory with 2G sensitivity would still enable significant advances in multimessenger science. The full case for an Australian observatory must be considered in a much broader context; however, this work indicates it could make substantial contributions to multimessenger astrophysics.

title: Toponium hadroproduction at next-to-next-to-leading order in NRQCD
summary: We present the first next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) predictions for inclusive color-singlet toponium hadroproduction within NRQCD in the zero-width limit for the top quark. The central new result is the NNLO QCD correction to the short-distance coefficient for pseudoscalar toponium production. The predictions include electroweak and relativistic corrections, additional production channels, and perturbatively evaluated bound-state matrix elements. At the Large Hadron Collider proton-proton center-of-mass energy of $13\,\mathrm{TeV}$, we obtain a cross section of $4.87^{+0.63}_{-0.65}\,\mathrm{pb}$, with scale and parametric uncertainties combined. The NNLO corrections reduce the renormalization- and factorization-scale uncertainties by approximately a factor of four relative to NLO, to the few-percent level. The dominant remaining uncertainty arises from the Coulomb-scale dependence of the bound-state matrix elements.

title: Non-local approximations for the Schrödinger operator with a general point interaction via the non-relativistic limit
summary: We consider the one-dimensional Dirac operator $D_{A,c}$ with a general, not necessarily self-adjoint, point interaction at the origin, whose strength is described by an arbitrary complex $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ and suitably rescaled by the speed of light $c$, together with its non-local approximations $D_{A,c}^ε$ obtained by replacing the Dirac distribution by a rank-one projection onto a scaled function $v_ε$. It is known that $D_{A,c}^ε\to D_{A,c}$ as $ε\to 0+$ and that $D_{A,c}-c^2/2$ converges, as $c\to+\infty$, to the Schrödinger operator $H_A$ with the general point interaction, both in the norm resolvent sense. We prove that the first convergence is uniform with respect to $c$ in a neighbourhood of $+\infty$, and we provide explicit rates of convergence. Combining this with an explicit computation of the non-relativistic limit of $D_{A,c}^ε$ for fixed $ε$, we show that the two limits can be interchanged and that the corresponding double limit exists. As a by-product we obtain a family of non-local, rank-two approximations $H_A^ε$ of $H_A$ that converge to $H_A$ in the norm resolvent sense. Contrary to the relativistic setting, the coupling constants of $H_A^ε$ are renormalized; we give an explicit formula for this renormalization.

title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
summary: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.

title: Repulsion-Driven Topological Superconductivity in Twisted MoTe$_2$
summary: We show that a microscopic model of twisted MoTe$_2$ with screened Coulomb interactions produces topological superconductivity. Using the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) on infinite cylinders, we find that the narrow Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ has Cooper pair correlations that strengthen with cylinder circumference, consistent with two dimensional superconductivity. The superconductor has chiral $f$-wave pairing around the valley center, and its topology produces chiral Majorana edge modes and non-Abelian vortex cores. At zero displacement field, the superconductor spans fillings $-0.78\lesssimν\lesssim-0.72$, close to the experimental range, and extends in a dome to finite displacement field. We then predict how its stiffness evolves with the filling and the tunable displacement field. The interplay with screening length is also examined. Nearby, we find a fractional Chern insulator, a topological charge density wave, a metal, and a charge-ordered state. The last is a candidate for the reentrant integer Hall regime in experiments. These results establish a route from repulsive interactions in microscopic models of moiré materials to chiral topological uperconductors with chiral Majorana edge modes.

title: Imaginary Time as a Complex Representation of Relativity
summary: We develop a systematic complex representation of Lorentzian relativity based on the imaginary temporal coordinate $X^0=ict$. Rather than treating this substitution as a Wick rotation to Euclidean spacetime, we formulate it as an invertible change of representation in which physical spacetime is identified with a real subspace of a complex vector space. This construction introduces two related metric structures: a complex-bilinear form and a Hermitian form, both of which reproduce the original Lorentzian interval when restricted to physical spacetime. We extend the representation to relativistic dynamics, including proper time, four-momentum, and the Hamilton-Jacobi formulation, and show that the metric, connection, curvature tensors, Einstein equations, and conservation laws retain their conventional content in curved spacetime. Explicit applications to the Kerr and Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker geometries demonstrate consistency for rotating and time-dependent spacetimes. We further examine relativistic wave equations and their nonrelativistic limit, showing how the Schrödinger equation and its relation to Euclidean-time evolution emerge within the same complex temporal framework. The resulting formulation introduces no new physical predictions, but clarifies the geometric role of imaginary temporal coordinates and reveals structural connections among relativistic geometry, action, wave propagation, and analytic continuation.

title: Shortcomings of the squark simplified model
summary: We argue that the squark simplified model commonly used in collider analyses fails to represent realistic low-energy supersymmetric models and significantly underestimates squark production rates at hadron colliders. This has important implications for extracting squark mass limits at the LHC and assessing the potential reach of HL-LHC or the FCC-hh. In particular, we find that the current LHC squark mass limit is realistically in the range of 2.6-3.0 TeV, rather than the 1.7-1.8 TeV range that is typically quoted based on the simplified model.

title: Dynamical Properties of the Multiple Elastic Pendulum
summary: This article studies the dynamical properties of the multiple elastic pendulum formed by an arbitrary number of point masses connected in a chain by elastic springs. First, using the Lagrangian formulation, the equations of motion governing the system's behavior, accounting for both large-angle displacements and elastic deformations, are derived. It is shown that well-established, low-dimensional systems, such as the classical double elastic pendulum, can be systematically recovered as particular cases directly from the general equations of motion after applying the appropriates particular conditions. The behavior of the system under small oscillations near its stable equilibrium is also investigated. For this case, the linearized equations allow the solution of the eigenvalue problem, demonstrating that in this case uncoupled behavior between the angular displacements and the spring elongations.

title: A lattice construction of the Kormos-Runkel-Watts defect flows in minimal models
summary: Kormos, Runkel, and Watts (KRW) showed that a topological defect of a diagonal minimal model $M(p,p+1)$, perturbed by a weakly relevant defect field, flows to a new conformal interface. We study the flow of the $(2,1)$ Verlinde defect $D_{(2,1)}$ driven by the spinful defect field $φ_{(1,3)}\otimes\barφ_{(3,3)}$ on the lattice. The flow preserves the $(r,1)$ Verlinde lines. This preserved symmetry makes a dilute RSOS realisation possible. We study this flow numerically using both exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). At $p=4$, the flow ends on the invertible line $η=D_{(3,1)}$. At $p=5$ it ends on a non-trivial conformal interface $C_5$ with $g=1.503(2)$ and transmission coefficient $T=0.665(10)$. We report its spectrum, leading irrelevant dimension, and lattice $β$-function. Gauging $η$ maps $C_5$ to an interface of the three-state Potts model, which breaks $\mathbb{Z}_3$ but is a stable interface once the Fibonacci line $τ_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ and charge conjugation are imposed. A loop-model formulation allows us to follow the family $C_p$ at continuous $4\le p\le5$: it moves smoothly from $C_5$ to $η$ as we lower $p$.

title: Lattice spin systems coupled to a compact U(1) gauge field with negative gauge coupling favoring frustration
summary: We investigate the phase diagram and nature of the phase transitions of three-dimensional compact lattice Abelian Higgs models with negative gauge coupling. These models describe multicomponent complex scalar fields coupled to a compact U(1) gauge field. Negative gauge coupling favors frustrated plaquette configurations, competing with the tendency of the matter ferromagnetic-like interaction to suppress frustration. Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analyses of models with one- and two-component scalar fields of unit charge reveal a substantially richer phase structure than at nonnegative gauge coupling. For two components, the O(3) transition line associated with gauge-invariant bilinear ordering extends into the negative-coupling region, and turns into a first-order transition line with decreasing $K$, toward the fully-frustrated $K\to -\infty$ limit. An analogous first-order transition line is also found for the one-component scalar matter with negative gauge coupling. Both one- and two-component models exhibit two additional continuous transition lines at sufficiently large matter coupling. Their energy-cumulant scaling is consistent with three-dimensional Ising and XY critical exponents, suggesting topological transitions in the $\mathbb Z_2$ and XY gauge universality classes, respectively. These results uncover additional phases generated by the competition between matter ordering and dynamical gauge frustration, whose physical characterization remains an open question.

title: Single-horizon regular black holes and the fate of the inner-horizon instability
summary: Regular black holes (RBHs) are often constructed with a regular point-like center and two horizons, including an inner Cauchy horizon susceptible to mass inflation. We show that a two-horizon structure is not a necessary consequence of regularity. For static, spherically symmetric geometries with an asymptotically static exterior, we establish a horizon-parity theorem: a regular point-like center requires an even number of sign-changing zeros of $f$. We then construct two classes of single-horizon RBHs with a finite-area core, distinguished by whether the horizon lies outside the core or coincides with it, and analyze their matter content, energy conditions, and thermodynamic properties. The absence of an inner Cauchy horizon eliminates the classical mass-inflation mechanism on the single-horizon patch. We further establish mode stability against scalar perturbations for these finite-area-core configurations by showing that the effective potential is non-negative. Our results establish how the central geometry and asymptotic structure constrain horizon multiplicity and identify single-horizon configurations that avoid the classical inner-horizon instability.

title: Modeling fragmentation of $^{20}$Ne nuclei at the LHC
summary: Fragmentation of relativistic neon nuclei was studied with the Abrasion-Ablation Monte Carlo for Colliders model (AAMCC-MST), which incorporates pre-equilibrium clustering of spectator matter via a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) algorithm, subsequent decays of the excited clusters, and Coulomb repulsion between final fragments. After validating the model against data on $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne fragmentation on various targets, the production of spectator nuclear fragments, neutrons, and protons in $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne collisions at the LHC was modeled at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$ TeV. The production cross sections, transverse and longitudinal momentum distributions for $^2$H, $^4$He, $^6$Li, $^{10}$B, $^{12}$C, $^{14}$N, and $^{16}$O fragments were calculated as these fragments may contaminate $^{20}$Ne beams circulating in the LHC. A simple parametrization describing relative width of the longitudinal momentum distributions calculated for these fragment species was constructed. To study the sensitivity of results to $α$-clustering and nuclear density distributions in neon nuclei, two density profiles for $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne were used: a deformed Woods-Saxon, and a five-$α$ bi-pyramidal configuration. In addition, a spherical profile was considered for $^{20}$Ne. Comparing results obtained with these profiles and with or without MST clustering shows that the calculated yields of spectator nucleons and fragments, their momentum distributions are sensitive to the details of nuclear structure of $^{20,22}$Ne and fragmentation modeling. The results provide the input for simulations of the transport of secondary forward nuclei in the LHC to estimate their interaction rates with circulating $^{20}$Ne beam nuclei, and also for calculations of responses of neutron and proton Zero Degree Calorimeters to $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne events.

title: Bayesian BiLO: Bilevel Local Operator Learning for Efficient Uncertainty Quantification of Bayesian PDE Inverse Problems with Low-Rank Adaptation
summary: Uncertainty quantification in PDE inverse problems is essential in many applications. Scientific machine learning and AI enable data-driven learning of model components while preserving physical structure, and provide the scalability and adaptability needed for emerging imaging technologies and clinical insights. We develop a Bilevel Local Operator Learning framework for Bayesian inference in PDEs (B-BiLO). At the upper level, we sample parameters from the posterior via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, while at the lower level we fine-tune a neural network via low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to approximate the solution operator locally. B-BiLO enables efficient gradient-based sampling without synthetic data or adjoint equations and avoids sampling in high-dimensional weight space, as in Bayesian neural networks, by optimizing weights deterministically. We analyze errors from approximate lower-level optimization and establish their impact on posterior accuracy. Numerical experiments across PDE models, including tumor growth, demonstrate that B-BiLO achieves accurate and efficient uncertainty quantification.

title: From off-shell strings to entropy flows
