summary: Bit threads express holographic entropy as the maximal flux of a divergenceless vector field subject to a local capacity bound, but do not identify a physical carrier of that flux. In our previous work, we identified the projected string charge density with a bit-thread flow, reproduced the entropies of BTZ and ten-dimensional three-charge black holes, and showed that the maximal entropy flux is preserved under S- and T-dualities. However, the norm bound was imported from the bit-thread prescription, while the string-current configurations were prescribed along known bit-thread lines. In this paper, we give a stringy foundation for the local capacity and construct dynamical probe-string representatives of maximal flow. At genus zero and two-derivative order, the conical variation of the target-space action derived from the off-shell sphere fixes the string-frame entropy density. The gravitational replica construction and weighted flow-cut duality then yield the string-frame norm bound. We next find regular stationary F1 solutions in an NS-NS supported BTZ black hole whose spatial parts are logarithmic spirals. A uniform ensemble produces a conserved, constant-norm projected string charge density and realizes a maximal flow whose flux equals the BTZ entropy. We finally extend the construction to BTZ backgrounds with mixed NS-NS and RR flux. Varying the flux fraction changes the stationary F1 configurations at fixed metric and dilaton, while the corresponding conserved flows reproduce the same leading BTZ entropy. Thus, both the norm bound and its physical maximal-flow representative arise from string theory, with stationary strings providing physical channels for the entropic flux represented geometrically by bit threads.

title: Possibility of Potts Spin-Ice in Rare Earth Twisted-Kagome Layers: an Example of DyAgGe
summary: Three-dimensional (3D) spin-ice compounds, predominantly based on the pyrochlore or spinel structure, have been attracting considerable interest in the last two decades. A two-dimensional (2D) analogue is the spin-ice consisting of kagome planes. So far, only Ising spin ice has been discovered in any material, and only one 2D material, the kagome compound HoAgGe, has been identified as a spin ice. In this Letter, we show that another rare-earth twisted Kagome magnetic compound, DyAgGe, is in fact a Potts spin ice (or color ice), where at each site not two but four spin directions are allowed. We argue that an 8-state spin ice may also exist in this class of systems. We present a first-principles calculation of magnetic interactions in DyAgGe, and confirm the 4-state Potts structure of this material by matching our model predictions with the available experimental data.

title: Late-time echoes from planar wave-packet scattering by an ultracompact star
summary: We simulate the propagation and scattering of an incident plane scalar wave in the spacetime of an ultracompact, horizonless constant-density star using a time-domain multipole mode-sum method. By reconstructing the coherently superposed time-domain waveforms, we compare the star's dynamical response with that of a Schwarzschild black hole. We find that the early-time response closely mimics a black-hole ringdown due to wave scattering near the exterior unstable photon sphere. Conversely, the late-time signal develops a sequence of delayed echoes originating from wave trapping near the interior stable light ring and subsequent leakage through the exterior potential barrier. While individual multipoles exhibit regular echoes, their coherent superposition induces interference, producing complex waveforms with irregular profiles that nonetheless retain an underlying temporal organization with alternating peak separations. Finally, as a proof of concept, we perform a signal-to-noise ratio analysis using an assumed strain normalization, demonstrating that these weak, late-time signatures can be resolved by third-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Multimuon Events from Cosmic Rays with the ALICE Detector
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, ISVHECRI2026, 5-10 July, 2026 Lecce, Italy
summary: ALICE experiment at the CERN's Large Hadron Collider, carried out a cosmic data-taking campaign in the period 2015-2018 (LHC Run 2), for a total of 62.5 days of real observation time. In this contribution, the analysis of these data is limited to multimuon events, i.e. events with more than four detected muons. In particular, the muon multiplicity distribution (MMD) is studied in the low-intermediate multiplicity range ($4 < N_μ < 50$), while for multiplicities $N_μ > 100$, dominated by large statistical fluctuations of the data, the rate of the high muon multiplicity events (HMM) is measured. The results are compared with Monte Carlo simulations using three of the main hadronic interaction models describing the air shower development in the atmosphere: QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC, and SIBYLL 2.3d, and assuming two extreme compositions of primary cosmic rays, pure proton and pure iron, representing respectively the lightest and the heaviest composition. Although the models have difficulty precisely describing the trend of primary p and Fe as a function of cosmic ray primary energy, QGSJET-II-04 is the only model that reproduces reasonably well the MMD and the rate of HMM events assuming a heavy composition for the entire energy range studied.

title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
summary: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

title: Exotic Pauli spinors and magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring
summary: We develop the formalism of the exotic Pauli equation and establish an effective symmetry between standard and exotic Pauli spinors to describe magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring within the nonrelativistic framework. We show that, once the signs of the spatial and temporal topological terms are fixed consistently by the covariant exotic Dirac equation, this symmetry is exact at the level of the equations of motion, Lagrangians and currents, with no truncation of the exotic term and no condition on the time dependence of the topological phase. Upon deriving the flux quantization condition, we explicitly construct the composite matter-gauge unitary operator acting on the Hilbert space, which implements the symmetry at the quantum level (the gauge sector requiring the usual regularization).

title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
summary: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. title: On mass inflation and late-time divergences in limiting-curvature regular black holes
summary: Mass inflation in non-extremal regular black holes with a non-linear dependence of the Misner-Sharp mass $M$ on the asymptotic mass $m>0$ may be a transient phenomenon followed by a model-dependent non-exponential late-time divergence. We analyse these regimes based on the generalised Ori model for a class of static spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat regular black holes with a de Sitter core and an $m$-independent upper bound on the Misner-Sharp mass density and Kretschmann scalar inspired by quasi-topological gravity. We discuss the geometric mechanism behind divergences of physical quantities at the inner horizon of the perturbed spacetime, and show that these require the unphysical mass parameter inside the shell to evolve outside the positive-real domain, or in some cases force a distinct type of dynamical continuation of the static metric. Imposing an asymptotic late-time divergence in form of a fractional power-law scaling, tunable to be arbitrarily mild within the considered approximation and effectively taming mass inflation, allows us to single out a family of generalised Fan-Wang regular black holes.

title: Pionization experiments in light nuclei
comment: To appear in Phys Rev C
summary: The zero-energy antiproton absorption in light nuclei is considered. The ratios $R_{n/p}$ of antiproton-neutron versus antiproton-proton capture rates in the lightest nuclei $^2$H, $^3$He and $^4$He are analyzed, both from the experimental results and from some selected theoretical models. These models are used as key input in determining the level shifts and widths of the lowest states. We establish the capture orbit in $^3$He to be states of angular momentum $L=2$. Several N-N optical potentials are used to compute the $R_{n/p}$ values for several heavy nuclei and the results are found to be consistent with the data. However, the old chamber experiments studying pionization in Helium, are not consistent with models. Only the Paris potential is likely to succeed provided baryonia states predicted by this model are better understood.

title: Fixed-grid schemes for fractional moving-boundary problems
summary: The Landau transformation xi = x/s(t) is the usual way to hold a moving boundary in place. It fails for fractional time derivatives because they have no chain rule: the transformed operator gains a nonlocal integral with a closed form only for self-similar fronts. We develop a sharp-interface finite-difference scheme for the conservation-consistent memory-flux fractional Stefan problem on a fixed grid, storing the memory limit h(x) = s^-1(x) as the time each node melts. The front is advanced using an integrated energy balance, with the singular source timed to the sub-step crossing instant. Against a known self-similar solution, the front constant is accurate to 0.02 to 0.11%, whereas competing formulations differ by 17 to 27% at alpha = 0.6. A remaining positivity violation follows from dt/t0 ~ s0^(1 - 2/alpha) and disappears on a front-locked time grid. We also derive two exact solutions with non-power-law fronts: a source-dominated solution and a Mittag-Leffler traveling wave, and verify the scheme against both. Neural-network solvers for moving boundaries are often trained in normalized coordinates; for alpha < 1, this silently changes the problem, while the change vanishes at alpha = 1, where checks are commonly performed. In the classical limit, our scheme is more accurate in 12 ms than a reimplemented moving-boundary network in 177 s.

title: Hamiltonian of open string field theory for time-dependent solutions
summary: Using the recently introduced expression for conserved charges of $L_\infty$ theories, we give an explicit form for the Hamiltonian of Witten's bosonic open string field theory. We evaluate it on the Erler-Maccaferri analytic solution, describing any D$p$-brane configuration associated to a BCFT. We use the expression to compute the energy of the rolling tachyon solution and find exact agreement with the boundary state result by Sen.

title: Stationary distribution of active Brownian particles in a bounded domain
summary:
Self-propelled particles such as swimming micro-organisms often accumulate at boundaries. Active Brownian particles (ABPs), that is, particles moving at constant speed with an orientation undergoing rotational diffusion, provide a simple model. ABPs have a finite probability to be on the boundary. Their probability density therefore includes both regular bulk and singular boundary components. Exchanges between these represent capture at the boundary and re-entry into the bulk.
  We examine the distribution of ABPs in the stationary regime. We first obtain a similarity solution that describes the probability density near the turning points, where orientation is tangential to the boundary and particles re-enter the bulk. This shows that the bulk density is singular and the boundary density is non-differentiable. We then add spatial diffusion to the ABP model and investigate the limit $\eps \to 0$ of small spatial diffusivity. We use matched asymptotics to describe the regularising effect of a finite $\eps$, focusing on the vicinity of the turning points. We assess our predictions against numerical simulations using both lattice Markov chain and finite-element discretisations.

title: On Isaacson's Procedure in $f(R)$-Gravity with Second Order Metric Perturbations
summary: In the recent paper arXiv:2504.02253 we generalized classical Isaacson's procedure for describing back-reaction of the averaged energy-momentum for high frequency gravitational waves to $f(R)$ gravity case with a choice of the de Sitter background. To describe this second order effect we used standard first order decomposition of metric tensor. In this paper, we take into account possible contribution to this process from second order term in metric tensor decomposition. We find that on the de Sitter background all possible contributions from this term are strongly suppressed and therefore results obtained in the paper arXiv:2504.02253 are left unchanged.

title: Schrodinger group along the horocycles and Egorov's theorem on compact hyperbolic surfaces
summary:
In this paper, we study Egorov's theorem for Laplacian eigenfunctions on compact hyperbolic surfaces in Zelditch's quantization. In this quantization, the remainder in Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is given explicitly by the second derivatives of the symbols along the weak stable foliation of the geodesic flow. Forward in time, we show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid to all logarithmic times, far beyond the Ehrenfest time T_E=|log h|/2, where h going to 0 is the semiclassical parameter.
  Backward in time, we introduce the Schrodinger group along the stable horocycles, which absorbs the exponentially growing part of the remainder. We show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid up to -T_E+T_h for any Th going to infinity with 0<=T_h<=T_E. Moreover, the limit of the remainder in Egorov's theorem at the Ehrenfest time -T_E is exactly the difference between the semiclassical measure and the Liouville measure, tested against the symbols propagated by the Schrodinger group. Consequently, Egorov's theorem for a sequence of eigenfunctions holds at -T_E (and in fact, at -T_E-T for any fixed T in R if and only if the sequence tends to be equidistributed in the phase space. Thus, the quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture is equivalent to this Egorov property holding for every eigenbasis. Furthermore, QUE holds with a polynomial rate if and only if Egorov's theorem holds at -T_E with a polynomial remainder. In this case, Egorov's theorem holds beyond -T_E with a polynomial remainder, and the stronger the rate is in QUE, the longer the time is in Egorov's theorem.

title: Obstruction to local entropy laws on arbitrary black-hole cuts in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
summary: We study local entropy laws on arbitrary cuts of event horizons in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, treated as an exact theory. No covariant local entropy can both reproduce the stationary black-hole entropy and be nondecreasing between every ordered pair of cuts, provided its density is smooth on an invariant open set of off-shell metric and cut jets containing a flat planar cut and every cut used in the argument. No global bound on derivative order is assumed. The counterexamples to the second law are vacuum black holes perturbed by a gravitational wave, with a strongly hyperbolic formulation near the relevant horizon interval and its stationary future. Shear makes the intrinsic curvature of a cut depend on its bending. The stationary entropy fixes the coefficient of this curvature term, and local corrections cannot cancel its response to cut bending. The obstruction appears at second order in wave amplitude on a smooth horizon, without a merger or topology change.

title: Liouvillian Kramers Degeneracy
summary: The Kramers theorem generally guarantees the spectral degeneracy of time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian operators with half-integer spin, underlying a variety of physical phenomena. Despite its fundamental significance, the Kramers degeneracy has been argued to be absent in Liouvillian superoperators acting on mixed states because of the double structure of the Hilbert space. Here, we instead demonstrate that the interplay of time-reversal symmetry$^†$ and parity symmetry enforces the Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillians. We explicitly construct dissipative many-body models of interacting fermions and spins exhibiting the Kramers degeneracy and show that their complex spectral statistics follow those of non-Hermitian random matrices in the corresponding symplectic symmetry classes. Of the three fundamental universality classes of non-Hermitian random matrices, the symplectic class has never been realized in symmetry-resolved many-body Liouvillians. Our constructions provide its explicit realizations and spectral signatures of nonintegrability in symplectic open quantum systems.

title: Final state of superradiant instability in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black hole
summary: This article examines the instability of charged black holes, using Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory and a massless charged scalar field. Our study demonstrates that these black holes become unstable in a certain range of frequencies, which causes scalar "hair" to form outside the event horizon. By using numerical integration on the coupled field equations, we show that there is a phase transition between a purely charged black hole and a hairy black hole configuration. The results show that the hairy phase appears when the temperature is less than $T_C$, the critical temperature, whereas for $T>T_C$, the system stays purely charged. Also, our findings show that the critical temperature increases with the size of the black hole, implying that the onset of the phase transition becomes progressively more difficult for larger horizons. Lastly, we see that the system enters a stable equilibrium at the critical temperature, which is the final state of the superradiant instability. These results provide us with useful information on how nonlinear superradiant events change and how scalarized black holes arise in more comprehensive theories of gravity.

title: Feynman Propagators on Exponentially Decaying Perturbations of Stationary Spacetimes with Compact Cauchy Surface
summary: In this paper, we construct Feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetime with compact Cauchy surface. The propagators are defined as parametrices of the wave operator on exponentially weighted Sobolev spaces defined by complex contours $Γ$. We then apply this theory to the computation of indexes of Dirac operators using a continuous Wick-like rotation to relate it to the Riemannian case.

title: Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the SU($N$) Thirring model at large $N$
summary: We investigate a Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Thirring model at leading order in $1/N$. We impose $f(\slashed{\partial})^\ddagger=f(\slashed{\partial})$ directly on the original action; for real nonlocality scale the admissible exponential choice is $f(\slashed{\partial})=\exp[-i\slashed{\partial}/Λ]$. We construct and analyze the even-in-mass (paired) large-$N$ effective potential and derive its radial kernel, weak-coupling dimensional-transmutation scale, and formal Lambert-$W$ zeros. Its radial gap integral possesses a conditionally convergent infinite-cutoff limit. The pairing prescription, however, differs from the unpaired determinant of the original Hermitian action, so the reported gap and spectral zeros must be understood as properties of this explicitly defined mean-field functional. We identify the further derivation needed to obtain physical mass gaps and fermion poles from the unpaired theory.

title: Effect of Small Particle Interactions on Assembly of Binary Colloidal Clusters
summary: A central challenge in colloidal self-assembly is understanding how interaction strength influences the competition between structural optimization and kinetic arrest during the formation of hierarchical structures. Here, we investigate the assembly process of a binary mixture of differently sized silica colloids dispersed in a near-critical water/2,6-lutidine solvent, where critical Casimir forces provide reversible and temperature tunable attractions. By systematically tuning the effective interactions between large-large (L-L), large-small (L-S), and small-small (S-S) particle pairs, we directly observe how the nucleation and growth of the binary colloid assemblies evolve in a wall-confined quasi-two-dimensional geometry when multiple pair-interactions are present. Confocal laser scanning microscopy imaging shows that combined L-L interactions and L-S interactions lead to compact L-S core-shell clusters with high shell occupancy, while the additional presence of S-S interactions suppress the shell formation and lead to extended, branched binary networks. Particle-resolved analyses of cluster growth and bond dynamics reveal that these structural transitions are governed by the motion of the small particles in the clusters changing from highly dynamic leading to structural reorganization to frozen dynamics resulting kinetic trapping. Our findings demonstrate how the interaction-governed mobility and kinetic arrest of small particles influence the growth of finite binary clusters and offers microscopic insight into the formation of binary crystals and kinetically trapped space-spanning binary colloidal networks and gels.

title: A Unified AI Framework for Rapid and Accurate Waveform Generation of Compact Binary Coalescences
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Supplementary material included
summary: The astrophysical discovery potential of future gravitational wave detectors will hinge on accurate and rapid waveform generation. Third generation detectors are expected to observe many long duration compact binary coalescence signals that can probe binary formation and evolution as well as the nature of matter under extreme conditions. We develop a unified framework that combines physical modeling with deep learning. The framework uses an analytic residual spectral representation, shared learning, and decoders for each binary type. It generates waveforms for binary black holes, binary neutron stars, and neutron star black hole binaries, providing a single unified generator for all compact binary coalescences. The generated waveforms include the physical effects described by each reference model, such as spin precession, higher order modes, matter effects, and postmerger radiation for binary neutron stars. The waveforms span hundreds to thousands of cycles, with mean mismatches ranging from $5.89\times10^{-4}$ to $5.34\times10^{-2}$ relative to the reference waveforms. Batch generation achieves a maximum speedup of about 1800 over reference waveform generation.

title: The Characteristic Initial Value Problem for the 3D Compressible Euler Equations
summary: We prove local existence and uniqueness, propagation of Sobolev regularity, and continuation criteria results for the characteristic initial value problem for the 3D compressible Euler equations. This is the Cauchy problem with initial data given on a pair of transversally intersecting (acoustically) null hypersurfaces. The region of existence in our main theorem is a future-neighborhood of the union of the data null hypersurfaces, where the size of the neighborhood depends on various norms of the data as well as the structure of the data null hypersurfaces. We allow for any equation of state with positive sound speed, and we do not make any symmetry, irrotationality, or isentropicity assumptions. Our analysis relies on the geometric formulation of the flow derived in [Speck19], which decomposes the equations into a "wave-part" coupled to a "transport-div-curl" part. Compared to Rendall's celebrated solution of the characteristic initial value problem for wave equations [Rendall90], substantial new ideas are needed to handle the fact that the compressible Euler equations are more complicated than pure wave equations.

title: A Ghost-Free dS/AdS Correspondence in $\mathcal{N}=1$ Supergravity
summary: Reversing the sign of the scalar potential exchanges de Sitter and anti-de Sitter vacua and, through the domain-wall/cosmology correspondence, maps flat domain walls onto flat FLRW cosmologies, but its supersymmetric version has ghosts on the cosmological side. We show that this pointwise correspondence is realized between two ordinary, ghost-free four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravities with spontaneously broken supersymmetry. Within a single superconformal Kähler cone, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ reflection of the nilpotent goldstino Kähler metric through the flat limit $V=0$ reverses $V\leftrightarrow-V$ pointwise while preserving the visible Kähler metric, the superpotential, and the unitary-gauge fermion Lagrangian. The paired vacua obey a sharp dictionary with $H=1/L$, $m^2_{\rm dS}=-m^2_{\rm AdS}$, equal conformal weights, and $m_{3/2}>H$, and are simultaneously stable precisely within the window $0\le m^2_{\rm dS}\le\frac94H^2$ set by the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound. Applied to string compactifications and cosmology, this correspondence pairs over-uplifted with under-uplifted anti-D3-brane vacua, confines the de Sitter swampland conjecture to the goldstino (anti-brane) sector, and maps slow-roll inflation onto a healthy AdS domain wall obeying the holographic $c$-theorem.

title: Early-age formation of MgO-SiO$_2$ binders and the effect of hydromagnesite and dehydrated hydromagnesite: An in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction and pair distribution function study
summary: MgO-SiO$_2$ binders are promising low-CO$_2$ alternatives to Portland cement that can permanently store CO$_2$ by incorporating magnesium carbonate phases. Adding a magnesium carbonate such as nesquehonite or hydromagnesite is known to change the initial hydration product from crystalline brucite (Mg(OH)$_2$) to disordered hydrous carbonate-containing brucite (HCB), yet how these binders evolve during the initial hours of reaction remains largely unknown. Here, in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) and pair distribution function (PDF) analysis follows an MgO-SiO$_2$ paste with and without hydromagnesite (HY, Mg$_5$(CO$_3$)$_4$(OH)$_2$$\cdot$4H$_2$O) or dehydrated hydromagnesite (DHY, HY heated at 325 °C to remove water) over the first 24 h, with ex situ measurements to 42 days. Real space phase quantification reveals that magnesium-silicate-hydrate (M-S-H) is detected in the first scan (~45 min) of every paste, before formation of any brucite or HCB. The PDF results also show that in the neat MgO-SiO$_2$ paste, half of the M-S-H present at 42 days has formed by 24 h, while no M-S-H is detected by XRD at any age due to the intrinsic disorder present in this phase. Both carbonate sources (HY and DHY) are found to increase the extent of MgO dissolution, where no unreacted MgO is detected at 24 h in contrast with >7 days for the neat paste. However, DHY is seen to slow the initial stages of MgO dissolution (prior to ~6 h) compared with the neat paste, a period during which significant DHY rehydration is seen to occur without any HCB formation. Hence, this investigation shows that the onset of HCB precipitation in MgO-SiO$_2$-(D)HY paste is influenced by the hydration state of the DHY phase, where precipitation is delayed while DHY is rehydrating.

title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
summary: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
summary: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

title: Negative Junction Logarithms in Scalar Multipartite Entanglement
summary: A three-region junction in a free real relativistic scalar vacuum in $2+1$ dimensions yields a strictly negative logarithmic contribution to genuine tripartite Rényi multi-entropy for every integer $n\geq3$ and all nondegenerate sector angles. The replica subtraction exactly removes loop classes associated with a single interface. Surviving loops have positive, scale-independent weight, yielding a logarithm whose sign is fixed by the negative Rényi prefactor. The selector is empty at $n=2$. The flat-sheet Friedrichs prescription fixes the scalar operator at the nonmanifold replica apex. It yields a convergent angular spectral formula for the coefficient.

title: Thermodynamically consistent thixotropic viscoelastic modeling of human blood from a conformational free energy
summary: Structural thixotropic viscoelastic models describe the rheology of human blood accurately, but their structural kinetics are postulated, so their compatibility with the second law of thermodynamics is not guaranteed. We present ROUGE (ROUleaux model Guided by free Energy), a tensorial model of blood that describes the deformation of individual red blood cells and of rouleaux with two conformation tensors, and the degree of aggregation with a scalar variable. A single postulated Helmholtz free energy determines the stress, the relaxation of all three variables, and the entropy generation, so the model satisfies the second law in any flow. To build it, we extend a simplified formulation of nonequilibrium thermodynamics, which accounts for conformational energy and entropy, to microstructures described by several structural variables of different kinds. The coupling between aggregation and rouleaux deformation is motivated by the Langmuir adsorption of fibrinogen and is restricted so that the quiescent, fully aggregated state is the stable minimum of the free energy. Fits to published data for step-ups and step-downs in shear rate show that the fibrinogen binding sites remain far from saturation, so that the free energy has no adjustable parameters. They also show that rouleaux breakdown requires no empirical shear-activation term: the structure is destroyed in proportion to the work done by the flow on the aggregates, and a single structural time produces both breakdown within seconds and an algebraic recovery over tens of seconds. The resulting model has five well-determined parameters, and its fitted solvent viscosity coincides with that of plasma.

title: On the Motion of a Point Electric Charge in the Field of Wu-Yang Monopoles in Bertotti-Robinson Spacetimes
summary: We study the $SU(2)$ Einstein-Yang-Mills system with non-minimal $RF^2$-type couplings of Yang-Mills fields to curvature, formulated with exterior differential forms and a Lagrange-multiplier constraint for the Levi-Civita connection. We show that the conformally flat Bertotti-Robinson geometry $AdS_2\times S^2$ carries the Wu-Yang magnetic pole as an exact solution for arbitrary non-minimal couplings; the couplings only renormalise the radius of the $S^2$. The non-conformally-flat branch of solutions known for this system is recalled. The Hopf fibration $S^3/S^2\cong S^1$ of the gauge group manifold projects the Wu-Yang field on a uniform Dirac-type magnetic field, and the motion of a point electric charge in it is solved in closed form: the charge moves on a cone and oscillates between the horizon and a maximal radius.

title: A note on the BRST-BV Formalism Explanation of Deformation Quantization and Algebraic Index Theorem
comment: 21 pages. AI is used for computations and English editing. Comments and suggestions are welcome!
summary: In this note, we begin with considering the simple one-dimensional field theory describing a single free particle on manifold, and apply the BRST formalism and BV quantization to this model following the standard procedures in physics. Through calculations that, while not fully rigorous, have a more transparent physical interpretation, then subsequent geometric identifications, we recover the deformation quantization and algebraic index theorem on symplectic manifold. This note thus elucidates the physical origins and mechanisms of these mathematical results.

title: On the universality of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory
summary: The standard definition of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory requires regularizing the entangling surface and factorizing the Hilbert space, which in turn involves a choice of boundary conditions at the regularized surface. This raises two natural questions which are open at present. The first is under what conditions there is a choice of boundary conditions that leads to a unitary map between the original Hilbert space and the factorized one, which is a necessary condition for a well-defined entanglement entropy. The second concerns the situation where there are multiple such choices, in which case the question is whether they all yield the same entropy, or at least the same terms usually referred to as universal. Focusing on topological theories and using three-dimensional Chern-Simons theory as a concrete illustration, we show under specified assumptions that different such choices affect only the non-universal terms in the entropy, such that the remaining terms are universal in this sense as well, while we explicitly demonstrate that boundary conditions corresponding to non-unitary maps can change these terms. We then explain how a similar argument applies to two-dimensional conformal field theories and discuss a condition for universality in general theories.

title: Constraining the Superconducting Gap of Monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$_3$ via Statistical Analysis and Tip-Height-Dependent Tunneling Spectroscopy
summary: Monolayer FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (001) exemplifies interface-enhanced superconductivity, exhibiting a transition temperature nearly ten times that of bulk FeSe. Yet, its tunneling spectra lack clearly identifiable superconducting coherence peaks, preventing an unambiguous determination of the gap magnitude. Here, we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy as a function of temperature, tip-sample separation, and lateral position to disentangle tunneling contributions by statistical analysis. Decay rates extracted by regression of tip-height-dependent spectroscopy reveal three energy regimes: Andreev-reflection-dominated tunneling below 6 meV, mixed Andreev and quasiparticle tunneling between 6 and 13 meV, and predominantly quasiparticle tunneling above 13 meV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy and correlation analysis further reveal that the tunneling conductance is predominantly localized near defects below 6 meV but becomes spatially extended at higher energies. Together, these results constrain the superconducting gap to lie between 6 and 13 meV. Our findings establish statistical analysis of spectroscopy as a powerful approach to constraining superconducting gap structures when complex spectral features prevent the unambiguous identification of coherence peaks.

title: Mixed-Order Parity-Violating Corrections to Rotating Black Holes in Combined Scalar Gauss-Bonnet and Dynamical Chern-Simons Gravity
summary: We construct the leading mixed-order $\mathcal{O}(ζ_{\rm GB}ζ_{\rm CS})$ deformation of rotating black holes in a combined scalar Gauss-Bonnet and dynamical Chern-Simons effective theory, the sector in which the parity-even and parity-odd corrections act simultaneously. Using a pseudospectral solution of the coupled mixed scalar and metric equations, we compute horizon and equatorial-geodesic observables--the horizon angular velocity, surface gravity, area, and Wald entropy; the innermost stable circular orbit and photon-ring radii; and photon-ring eikonal estimates of the ringdown--at fixed mass and angular momentum over the spin range $0.1\le a\le0.9$, where the solution is numerically convergent and the perturbative expansion is controlled for sufficiently small dimensionless couplings. We verify the exact Kerr and Schwarzschild limits, reproduce available pure-sector benchmarks, and quantify spectral, residual, and extraction uncertainties. The mixed solution satisfies every component of the field equations, including the one that is not imposed in its construction, and its Wald entropy satisfies the first law to about one part in $10^{5}$. The mixed coefficients exhibit spin dependence qualitatively distinct from the individual sectors within this EFT truncation. All four horizon quantities, and several orbital and eikonal ones, change sign as functions of spin. The ringdown results are leading photon-ring eikonal estimates; a full coupled finite-$\ell$ perturbation calculation is left to future work.

title: Scaling laws for linear-elastic two-variant martensitic phase transitions in general domains
summary: We consider a two-well problem within geometrically linear elasticity, on a bounded Lipschitz set in dimension $n\ge 2$. We assume that the two wells are compatible through a symmetrized rank-one connection and that the displacement matches their average on the boundary, and we include a regularization based on the total surface energy. We show that there are two distinct regimes, with the energy scaling differently in terms of the surface-energy coefficient $\eps$: it is proportional to $\eps^{2/3}$ if there are two distinct compatible twin-normal directions, and to $\eps^{4/5}$ if there is only one. This matches previous findings in rectangles and other special geometries, mostly in two dimensions, and the lower bounds obtained by a Fourier method by Raiţă, Rüland, Tissot and Tribuzio (2024). Our results are obtained by explicit constructions, which contain a self-similar refinement of oscillations close to the boundary, and by a short real-space proof of the matching lower bounds.

title: Gauge-invariant thermodynamic description of rotating black strings in 5D minimal supergravity via Kaluza-Klein reduction
summary: We develop a gauge-invariant formulation of the thermodynamics of rotating black strings in five-dimensional minimal supergravity through Kaluza-Klein reduction. At the two-derivative level, we consistently reduce the bulk action and the Gibbons-Hawking-York boundary term, carefully accounting for the surface contributions induced by the Chern-Simons coupling. The resulting four-dimensional theory is $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity coupled to a single vector multiplet, with prepotential $P=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\frac{X_1^3}{X_0}$. Employing the Hamiltonian formalism, we establish the quantum statistical relation between the Euclidean on-shell action and the Gibbs free energy. We further compute the leading four-derivative corrections to the thermodynamics of a rotating magnetic black string using the Reall-Santos method. The resulting corrections are in precise agreement with previous results obtained directly for the Kerr-Newman black hole in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity.

title: Korringa factor in Dirac-nodal-line systems
summary: The Korringa factor $K(α)$ in the nuclear magnetic resonance studies is a widely used measure of electron-correlation effects in metals and is conventionally interpreted using the non-correlated value $K(α)$ = 1. In Dirac-fermion systems, however, the non-correlated reference value depends on the electronic density of states (DOS) and differs from that of conventional metals. Here, we theoretically investigate the non-correlated Korringa factor $K^*(α)$ in a Dirac nodal-line (DNL) system with finite nodal-line dispersion using a DOS-based approach. We show that $K^*(α)$ exhibits an intrinsic temperature dependence, continuously evolving from the Dirac-fermion value of 1.71 at high temperatures to the metallic value of 1 at low temperatures. The crossover temperature is found to be proportional to the nodal-line dispersion width, identified as the characteristic energy scale governing the non-correlated Korringa factor in DNL systems. We further demonstrate that Landau quantization generates singular DOS structures that strongly enhance $K^*(α)$, producing pronounced peaks even in the absence of electron correlations. In addition, $K^*(α)$ exhibits two distinct types of magnetic oscillations arising from intra-level and inter-level contributions. The latter originates from the overlap of singular points belonging to positive and negative quantum-number Landau subbands at the Fermi level and represents a unique consequence of the finite energy dispersion of a DNL. These results provide a quantitative reference for interpreting NMR experiments in DNL materials and for identifying genuine correlation effects beyond DOS-induced contributions.

title: Scale-Dependent Weak-Field Dynamics in Horndeski Theory: Galaxy Rotation Curves and Turnaround Scales
summary: In this work, the weak-field dynamics of a gravitational-wave compatible subclass of Horndeski gravity is investigated on galactic and intergalactic scales. The analysis is performed within the weak-field approximation for stationary and approximately spherically symmetric configurations, retaining the nonlinear scalar derivative interactions responsible for scale-dependent modifications of the gravitational field. On galactic scales, the transition regime is investigated through the effective potential, the stability of circular orbits, galaxy rotation curves, and the relation between dynamical and lensing masses. The analysis shows that the scalar field modifies the orbital dynamics and the radial dependence of the rotational velocity, while generating a nonvanishing gravitational slip between the dynamical and lensing mass estimates. On intergalactic scales, the asymptotic weak-field dynamics is investigated and a turnaround scale is derived from the balance between the effective gravitational attraction and the large-scale curvature contribution. At large distances, the asymptotic gravitational field is governed by the background curvature contribution.

title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
summary: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.

title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
summary: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet inflation. Starting from the quadratic perturbation actions, we construct the two-mode Hamiltonians and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing amplitudes and angles. Although the tensor speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss--Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We track the squeezing dynamics from the subhorizon to the superhorizon regime and evaluate the Nielsen wave-function complexity of the resulting two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation in the squeezing amplitudes, while the unwrapped squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Consequently, the circuit complexity is controlled mainly by the amplitude evolution. A positive coupling enhances the scalar complexity but slightly suppresses the tensor complexity for the benchmarks considered. These opposite trends show that scalar and tensor Gaussian states retain distinct information about the same modified inflationary background even when tensor propagation is luminal.

title: Maximum entropy explanation for the ubiquity of power-law mechanical responses
summary: The ubiquitous power-law relaxation emerges from complex mechanical systems with a vast number of interacting exponential responses. Here we demonstrate that power-law responses satisfy a maximum entropy criterion, regulating the individual contributions under partial knowledge. This leads to a prediction that frequency range of validity decreases with power-law exponent, a property which is confirmed for some biological materials. The close relation with the fractional standard linear solid also leads to an incorporation of the equally ubiquitous stretched exponential behavior.

title: Gravitational-wave lensing beyond the diffraction integral: proper-time methods and the bound lens
summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) can have wavelengths comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of their lenses, and detectors record their phase, so lensing requires wave optics. Its standard tool, the diffraction integral, follows from the particle path integral of a scalar wave on a static weak field, under the eikonal (one-way) and paraxial approximations, plus the thin-lens limit. We give a self-contained account of how the proper-time (worldline) representation overcomes these steps. An auxiliary proper time makes the wave equation exactly first order, with frequency as $1/\hbar$, so geometric optics and, for paraxial thin-lens paths, the diffraction integral follow from stationarity of an exact integral. For a point mass, the Duru-Kleinert (DK) gauge and Kustaanheimo-Stiefel map give the exact propagator; for a distant observer the DK time and fibre angle become the radius and azimuth of a lens plane, the result is the point-lens amplification factor with the offset set by the excess path, and geometric optics requires $w\gg1$ and $wy\gg1$. This agreement reflects the Coulomb potential, not the approximations: the exact eikonal condition, $\varepsilon_E\simeq\barλ/d+GM/c^2d+\mathcal O(\sin^2θ/2)$, fails near the lens and at large angles, and the one-way step is a non-relativistic limit. We then treat the bound lens, a GW source orbiting its lens, which emits a backscattered echo and moves during the lensing delays. Its exact time-domain signal gives each worldline its own retarded time and Doppler factor, so no single amplification factor describes it. In the diffraction regime the Shapiro phase alone misses all lensing beyond it, geometric optics misses 46-100% of it near conjunction at $w=0.3$, the paraxial geometry fails on the far side, and the static amplification factor along the orbit errs by $\approx(1-2)\,wM/R$ near conjunction and by the echo amplitude elsewhere.

title: Weak uniqueness and autonomous approximation for the SLE-reversible Weil-Petersson response diffusion
summary: We study the self-consistent common-noise equation associated with the Weil--Petersson response differential of the rotationally marked SLE welding probability. For $0<κ\leq4$, we prove joint weak uniqueness among continuous adapted weak solutions whose law at each deterministic time is the welding probability, and obtain the Markov property in the original filtration. A conditional Gaussian lift and capacity localization give the required $L^1$ generator-range density. Identification with the canonical law gives stationarity and reversibility. We also construct autonomous Fejér and Poisson regularizations with pathwise-unique global strong solutions. Their joint state-noise laws converge to the canonical law for every initial probability absolutely continuous with respect to the welding probability.

title: Regge bounds and eikonal scaling in a four-dimensional scalar EFT
summary: Positivity bounds rest on twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which assume that the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partialφ)^4/Λ^4$ and $g_6(\partialφ)^6/Λ^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. The same construction is applied in the forward limit required by the dispersion relation, and we use the one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff to constrain $g_4$ and $g_6$.

title: Triboelectric nanogenerators across length scales: linking materials, multiscale modelling and applications
summary: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) convert low-frequency mechanical energy into electricity and enable self-powered sensing. Their performance depends on interactions among material properties, surface morphology, contact mechanics, charge generation and external circuits. This review examines these interactions across length scales to assess how material and interface descriptions support predictive device design. Polymeric, inorganic, composite and natural materials are discussed in relation to charge generation and retention, mechanical compliance, durability and application requirements. Modelling approaches span molecular dynamics and first-principles calculations, rough-surface contact mechanics, device-scale electrostatics and equivalent circuits. Their capabilities are assessed through the inputs they require, the quantities they predict and the experimental evidence used for validation. Particular attention is given to prescribed surface charge density, idealised geometries and nominal contact-area assumptions, which constrain predictions under realistic loading conditions. Applications are organised by macroscale, milliscale and microscale device dimensions to examine requirements for materials, architecture and integration. The review identifies evolving real contact area and contact-dependent charge generation and decay as critical links between interfacial behaviour and electrical output. A staged validation strategy is proposed for contact mechanics, electrostatics and circuit response, with independent testing beyond calibration conditions. These priorities guide the development of multiscale models and reliable TENG systems.

title: Excitation factors and exceptional points of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes
summary: We study excitation factors and investigate exceptional points (EPs) of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes using the exact separated gravitoelectromagnetic equations. At fixed charge, the magnitudes of the excitation factors for the gravitational-led modes studied here decrease with increasing spin, whereas those for electromagnetic-led modes exhibit both monotonic and nonmonotonic behavior. The magnitude of the excitation factor for the first overtone can be comparable to or larger than that for the fundamental mode. We identify 42 EPs at which pairs of modes coalesce in the gravitational-led and electromagnetic-led sectors. Some EPs form sequences involving successive overtone pairs, with higher-overtone pairs coalescing progressively closer to the extremal limit. The additional EPs identified outside these sequences all share the same mode-pair labels as sequence members, but occur at different values of the black hole spin and charge. These findings clarify how rotation and charge shape the relative excitation strengths of different modes and the pattern of mode coalescence in the non-Hermitian spectrum of Kerr--Newman black holes.

title: Uniqueness in an incompressible fluid with objective heat conduction model
summary: In the context of heat conduction, the equations of Maxwell-Cattaneo is a successful alternative to the Fourier's law. In 2009, Christov proposed a frame-independent (or objective) generalization of Maxwell-Cattaneo equation. For a more general class of objective heat conduction Maxwell-Cattaneo-Christov equations proposed by Angeles, a uniqueness result is proved, applied to an incompressible fluid.

title: Modular properties of correlators in generalised Gibbs ensembles
summary: We study the modular properties of torus correlators in a generalised Gibbs ensemble (GGE) of a two-dimensional conformal field theory. For the free fermion with KdV charges, we compute the exact two-point function and derive its modular $S$-transformation as a formal power series in the chemical potential. The transformed correlator admits a factorised description: an effective charge deforms the ensemble, while a local dressing operator acts on the external fields. Both are determined by nested operator product expansions involving the deforming current. Motivated by this result, we conjecture an analogous transformation law for $n$-point functions in rational chiral conformal field theories. Using Zhu's recursion, we establish the conjecture at the lowest explicit power of the modular parameter to all orders in the chemical potential, thereby determining the dressing operator. We also verify the full conjectured transformation through cubic order in the chemical potential, retaining all explicit powers of the modular parameter. These results extend the nested-OPE description of modular transformations of GGE partition functions to local correlation functions.

title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
summary: We propose a scheme to realize Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial bands in the strongly correlated regime of a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and strong Hubbard interaction. Spin-flip hopping suppressed by the large Zeeman detuning is resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, yielding a correlated spin-orbit coupling that depends on the local particle configuration. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning the interaction strength and particle filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold $^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results highlight density-assisted spin-orbit coupling as a mechanism for realizing Weyl superfluidity in strongly correlated systems.

title: Full-Stokes response to a stochastic gravitational-wave background in pulsar timing arrays: Fully analytic overlap reduction functions at finite distance and coherence of close pulsar pairs
summary: We derive fully analytic overlap reduction functions for the full-Stokes response of a pulsar timing array to an anisotropic tensor gravitational-wave background in general relativity. The response retains both pulsar distances and their complete propagation phases. At each fixed finite sky multipole, the intensity and circular polarization responses reduce to finite combinations involving exponential integrals and logarithms, while the electric and magnetic linear polarization responses require only elementary functions. We evaluate all components through $\ell=8$. Symmetry separates exact nulls from additional Earth-term nulls that propagation can lift. Even an unpolarized background can produce an imaginary cross-spectrum. For a pair with three-dimensional separation $d$, the pulsar terms can remain coherent when $2πfd/c\lesssim1$, even if both pulsars are many wavelengths from Earth. A uniform approximation retaining all four Earth and pulsar terms connects this regime to the short-wavelength limit, and a rotationally invariant relation fixes the leading transverse magnetic response. Common-distance errors cancel from the aligned pair phase, while relative-depth errors directly affect coherence. Under Gaussian differential averaging, fixed low-multipole norms and the squared norm summed over all multipoles decay at different rates as the response shifts to higher multipoles. Published pulsar configurations illustrate the roles of distance accuracy, bandwidth, and timing fits. At fixed pointwise intensity, a polarization covariance bound and a relative-depth noise budget quantify when differencing suppresses the background. Independent sky integration and matched-accuracy benchmarks test the analytic expressions over the parameter ranges studied.

title: Stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations
summary: The aim of this article is to derive a stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations, based on the location uncertainty principle (LU). Next, these equations are used to infer simpler models from scaling limits, such as the Saint-Venant, Boussinesq and Serre-Green-Naghdi ones. Once adapted to the stochastic setting, these models have been successfully implemented numerically, and we show several experiments to assess their properties -- for example the breaking of the wave symmetry, and the influence of time correlated noises.

title: Scalar radiation from circular orbits in D3 brane spacetimes: a Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi-like approach
summary: We study scalar perturbations in a ten-dimensional D3 brane spacetime, developing a (higher-dimensional) Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi-like formalism adapted to the present case leading to a sourced modification of a Mathieu equation. As an application, we compute the energy loss both at infinity and at the horizon in terms of scalar waves due to a scalar charge moving along a circular "equatorial" geodesic.

title: Energy-Resolved Cross-Correlation of THz Field Emission of Electrons from a Metal Nanotip
summary: Intense THz pulses, combined with the lightning-rod field enhancement at metal nanotips, can drive field emission of keV-energy, femtosecond-duration electron bunches, yet the dynamics governing this emission remain largely unexplored. Here we probe these dynamics by cross-correlating the energy-resolved emission driven by two independently generated single-cycle THz pulses focused onto a tungsten nanotip, scanning their relative delay over 160 ps. At total bunch charges approaching $10^6$ e$^-$, the delay-energy emission map near zero delay reveals electrons accelerated up to 2.1 keV, with a cross-correlation width of ~210 fs full width at half maximum at the highest energies. Apart from replicas caused by optical reflections in the setup, no emission echoes are observed over the full delay range, ruling out long-lived antenna resonances such as Sommerfeld-wave reflections along the tip shaft. A 1D Fowler-Nordheim model incorporating a low-$Q$, sub-picosecond antenna response for the local field enhancement reproduces the peak electron energies and the asymmetry of the delay-energy map. Our results indicate that each THz pulse produces a single, isolated electron burst, and that energy filtering can select its shortest, highest-energy component.

title: Dirac stars in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg theory
summary: We study self-gravitating configurations of a charged classical spinor field coupled to gravity and to Euler-Heisenberg (EH) nonlinear electrodynamics, truncated at quartic order. The spinor is gauged under a U(1) field and may carry a quartic self-interaction. For static and spherically symmetric configurations we derive the field equations, reduce them to a dimensionless eigenvalue problem for the spinor frequency and solve it numerically. In the uncharged limit our solutions coincide with the known Dirac stars of general relativity. The electric charge increases the frequency, the mass and the size of the stars, and the maximal mass grows from $0.709$ to $1.027$ (in units of $M_{\rm Pl}^2/μ$) when the charge coupling rises from zero to $0.75$. The quartic term changes the relation between the electric field and the enclosed charge, so that the field inside the star is weaker than in the Maxwell case. Our central result concerns stars with the same number of fermions, and therefore the same total charge. For them the quartic term changes the mass by less than $0.2\%$, but it makes the stars more compact and more strongly bound and shifts the turning point of the family to a smaller particle number. This shift is what lowers the maximal mass, by $9\%$ (from $0.924$ to $0.840$) at charge coupling $0.6$ as the dimensionless EH coupling goes from zero to $200$. In the weak-field regime of quantum electrodynamics (QED) the relative mass correction is $-1.5\times10^{-5}(E_{\max}/E_c)^2$, so the larger couplings describe the quartic model as an effective nonlinear electrodynamics rather than a controlled QED correction. All solutions satisfy the null, weak, strong and dominant energy conditions, show a positive pressure anisotropy, and remain free of horizons. Their stability is discussed through the binding energy and the turning point of the mass curve.

title: Hidden Symmetries of the Kepler Problem and Jacobi's Theorem
summary: We present a geometric derivation of the hidden symmetries of the Kepler problem, combining a duality for central-force systems, obtained by interchanging positions and velocities, with a generalized form of Jacobi's theorem. Applied to the dual Kepler problem, this theorem identifies Kepler hodographs of prescribed energy with geodesics of a metric of constant curvature. After adjoining one point at infinity, the resulting geometry is complete. Its Killing vector fields induce a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries on the corresponding energy hypersurface. The distinguished point at infinity determines a canonical decomposition of the Killing algebra into two vector subspaces, whose associated Noether invariants recover angular momentum and the Runge-Lenz vector.

title: The Stringy Origin of Kerr Multipoles
summary: We construct a new family of exact open and closed bosonic string solutions in flat spacetime that reproduce the root-Kerr and Kerr multipoles at every fixed multipole order in the large-mass and large-angular-momentum limit. These solutions provide explicit classical data for identifying associated quantum string states and testing their correspondence with rotating black holes.

title: Dynamical Phonon Anharmonicity Drives Charge-Density-Wave Softening and Electronic Quasiparticle Decoherence in Monolayer 1H-NbSe2
summary: Charge-density-wave (CDW) instabilities in two-dimensional materials are governed by strongly anharmonic soft phonons, whose dynamical behavior remains poorly understood beyond the statically renormalized vibrations. Here, using monolayer 1H-NbSe2, we investigate how frequency-dependent three- and four-phonon interactions reshape phonon spectral functions and influence electronic excitations. We find that three-phonon interactions induce substantial dynamical softening of CDW modes, increasing the estimated transition temperature relative to static self-consistent phonon theory. Four-phonon interactions further promote such dynamical softening and enhance spectral broadening, producing non-Lorentzian lineshapes that challenge the quasiparticle picture. Incorporating dynamically renormalized phonon frequencies and electron-phonon coupling into Fan-Migdal electron self-energy calculations reveals enhanced electronic kinks, satellite features, and momentum-dependent quasiparticle decoherence, driven by the strong momentum dependence of the electron-phonon coupling matrix elements. These findings establish dynamical anharmonicity as a critical link between soft-mode lattice fluctuations and electronic spectral signatures, providing insights into coupled lattice-electron dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.

title: Kerr metric perturbations in Lorenz gauge via numerical relativity methods
summary: Gravitational self-force calculations are needed to accurately describe the motion of a small body in a spinning (Kerr) black hole spacetime, which is vital to predict gravitational wave signals from asymmetric-mass compact binaries. Accurate calculations for the upcoming LISA mission require a minimum of second perturbative order in the mass ratio, which has thus far only been achieved for nonspinning (Schwarzschild) black holes due to nonlinear complexities of the Einstein equations. In this work, we calculate Kerr metric perturbations with a new computational approach based on numerical relativity methods, extending recent scalar self-force results to full general relativity. We formulate the perturbative Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in terms of azimuthal $m$-modes in the frequency domain and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using a spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers. With our new method, we achieve exponentially convergent first-order gravitational self-force calculations for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to spin $|a|/M=0.998$ (the Thorne limit). Our framework is designed to carry over to second order by delivering accurate and well-behaved first-order data for nonlinear source construction, and as a solver for the second-order metric perturbations themselves.

title: Exponential decay for the two-dimensional Heisenberg model
summary:
In this work, we prove exponential decay for the spin correlation of the spin $O(\mathsf{N})$ model for $\mathsf{N}\geq3$ at every inverse temperature $ β>0 $. In particular, our work confirms Polyakov's prediction in 1975 on the Heisenberg model, i.e., the case of $\mathsf{N}=3$.
  To this end, we investigate a generalized $O(\mathsf{N})$ model where $ \mathsf{N} $ is a positive \emph{real number}, as follows: we sample a loop soup on the metric graph (say of a box) with intensity $ \tfrac{\mathsf{N}}{2} $ subject to the conditioning that the local time at each lattice vertex is $β$, and then for each loop we independently assign it to copies $1\leq \mathsf{i}\leq \lceil\mathsf{N}\rceil$ such that it is assigned to copy $\mathsf{i}$ with probability $ \tfrac{1}{\mathsf{N}} $ for $ 1\leq \mathsf{i}\leq \lfloor\mathsf{N}\rfloor $. Then, by Lupu's isomorphism theorem, we can construct a spin field by assigning a random sign to each loop soup cluster in each copy independently, such that the field coincides with the spin $O(\mathsf{N})$ model when $\mathsf{N}$ is an integer. We then establish exponential decay for every real-valued $\mathsf{N}>2$. Our result reveals an underlying mechanism for exponential decay, which emerges as soon as $\mathsf{N}>2$ (i.e., as soon as beyond the range of the XY model) and does not necessarily rely on the rotation symmetry in the sphere $ \mathbb{S}^{2} $.

title: Fortuitous BMN Operators from Multiple Cores
summary: We develop a systematic construction of fortuitous cohomology classes in the BMN sector of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory from multiple lower-rank building blocks. For arbitrary partitions of colour space, we construct corrected effective letters that obey the supersymmetry transformations of the corresponding lower-rank theories. These allow us to build gauge-invariant, $Q$-closed polynomial operators. A restriction map recovers the constituent cohomology classes, establishing non-exactness and fortuity without brute-force computations. As an explicit example, we combine two fortuitous $SU(2)$ cores to construct a fortuitous class in $SU(4)$. Our results provide a systematic approach to the structure of fortuitous cohomology at finite $N$.

title: Continuum Dirac Theory and Nonlinear Extensions of a Chain of Alternating non-linear springs: an SSH version of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model
summary: A mechanical version of the SSH model, made of equal masses joined by two alternating non-linear springs is studied in the continuum limit. Such a non-linear dimerized mechanical chain generates a nonlinear, dispersive, two-field hyperbolic system of Boussinesq type of differential equations, describing coupled acoustic and gapped optical fields. The corresponding Lagrangian density is found, revealing that the acoustic and optical degrees of freedom are coupled through a structure that is formally analogous to a synthetic spin-orbit coupling, where the spatial motion is locked to the internal sublattice degree of freedom. An emergent non-Abelian Berry connection term also appears. Some particular solitary-wave solutions are found using variational theory, as the effective optical field obeys an undamped and unforced cubic-quintic Duffing equation. Near the Brillouin-zone edge, the system becomes a nonlinear Dirac field theory of the Soler type, providing a direct mechanical realization of interacting relativistic solitons. By factoring out fast spatial oscillations, an effective Jackiw-Rebbi Hamiltonian is obtained, with topological zero modes at domain walls. These modes are akin to the electronic flat bands in moire graphene systems associated with superconductivity and charge fractionalization. Finally, we discuss the mechanical rigidity transition and its effects on the fields as the system evolves toward the fully dimerized limit, in which the zero modes are floppy modes.

title: The Nonlinear Physics and Statistical Field Theory of Twilight Clouds: Hovering Dynamics and Dynamic Inertia Emergence
summary: Twilight clouds are small, optically faint warm clouds whose droplets fluctuate between haze and activated growth. We develop a nonequilibrium statistical field theory linking this regime to cloud-field organization through Köhler microphysics, supersaturation transport, and turbulent mixing. At parcel level, supersaturation rapidly tracks slow droplet growth with a finite lag. Mixing-induced supersaturation removal drives a saddle-node bifurcation, shifting the activation threshold and supporting intermittent hovering under turbulent fluctuations. Starting from turbulent transport of supersaturation coupled to droplet growth, we derive a droplet-supersaturation field system and formulate it within the Martin-Siggia-Rose framework. A Gurari-type variational reduction inspired by polaron theory eliminates the fast bath. Turbulence dresses the slow droplet field, shrinks the forbidden zone below the equilibrium curve, and raises the mixing threshold required to suppress activation. Each droplet population induces a screened supersaturation halo that couples neighboring cloud elements; its delayed adjustment generates dynamic inertia and temporally correlated noise. The resulting nonlinear, non-Markovian pseudoparabolic stochastic equation has a bounded frozen-background response at short wavelengths. Its long-wave coupling amplifies contrasts where the dressed slow manifold turns downward. Comparisons with the parent two-field system show that a spatially correlated Markovian closure preserves droplet-radius distributions and cloudlet organization. Near the activation fold, restoring residual-bath fluctuation memory improves recurrent-hovering frequency and patch extent without recalibrating the drift or fitting a correlation time. More broadly, the framework identifies how slow fields acquire interactions and inertia through the relaxing, diffusive environments they modify.

title: Crossover from Schwarzian dynamics to rotational soft modes in near-extremal Lovelock black holes
summary: Near-extremal black holes are controlled by a small set of soft modes, and counting these modes fixes the coefficient of $\log T$ in the entropy. We ask whether genuine six-derivative interactions change that count, working in seven-dimensional third-order Lovelock gravity, the simplest setting where the cubic Lovelock term is dynamical. The multiplicities stay the same, but the naive count fails. At fixed charge the Maxwell mode is frozen out, and the fifteen rotational modes of the $S^5$ act as a quantum rotor that only switches on above the scale $K_J^{-1}$. As a result, the coefficient of $\log T$ runs from $3/2$ at the lowest temperatures to $9$ above that scale, and never reaches the naive Gaussian value $19/2$. We compute the moment of inertia $K_J$ from the charged slow-rotation solution and find that the Lovelock couplings move the crossover without changing the multiplicities. Only large AdS black holes have a wide window in which the full rotational contribution competes with the classical entropy. Adding a probe charged scalar, we derive an analytic near-horizon Schwinger threshold in the cubic coupling. Its large-AdS limit tells us when the broad rotational crossover window can coexist with the absence of a charged-scalar Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound violation.

title: Resolving magnetic order and dynamics with polarized neutron scattering: a practical guide to longitudinal polarization analysis
summary: Neutron scattering provides microscopic information on magnetic order and spin dynamics. Most experiments, however, use unpolarized neutrons and do not fully exploit the information carried by the neutron spin. Longitudinal polarization analysis (LPA), established in the pioneering work of Moon, Riste, and Koehler at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the late 1960s, separates magnetic and nonmagnetic scattering contributions through their different effects on the neutron spin. In this review, we illustrate how LPA can distinguish weak magnetic scattering from nonmagnetic contributions, constrain small moment components, and resolve the spin-space anisotropy of magnetic excitations. We introduce the formalism connecting measured polarization channels to magnetic quantities and discuss scattering geometry, crystallographic projections, and corrections for finite polarization. Our aim is to provide a practical guide for neutron scatterers using LPA to determine magnetic structures and characterize spin excitations in quantum materials. We conclude with opportunities in altermagnets, unconventional superconductors, and kagome magnets.

title: Pure Spinor Factorization of Belinski-Zakharov Solitons and Regular Gravitational Instantons
summary: We show that the Belinski-Zakharov soliton construction factorizes into signed Pfaffian tau-functions, revealing a pure-spinor description of the metric and its regularity conditions. We derive analytic restrictions on the integral rod data, prove uniqueness for the asymptotically flat balance problem at fixed rod structure and periods, and give a conditional criterion for global existence. Combining these results with exhaustive enumeration of the admissible data and rigorous existence certificates, we construct a catalogue of regular asymptotically flat solutions representing 356 rod-word classes through twelve turning points, and 52 isolated regular asymptotically locally flat solutions through eight turning points. Analytic positivity and smooth-completion results establish regularity beyond the finite numerical solve. Based on this catalogue, we investigate two organizations of the solution space: generalized rank-two root systems and compositions of simpler endpoint geometries. The endpoint composition rules reproduce exactly all retained asymptotically flat words through twelve turning points.

title: Almost primes in short intervals and averages of long Dirichlet polynomial approximations to $(ζ'/ζ)^{k}$
summary: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the mean square of long truncations of the Dirichlet series for $\bigl(ζ'/ζ\bigr)^{k}$ on the critical line; we establish the connection between this problem and the short-interval variance of the convoluted von Mangoldt function $Λ^{*k}$ in short intervals and in arithmetic progressions. Under a shifted moments conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), we prove that the short-interval variance leading coefficient is the derivative of the mean-square leading coefficient. A unitary trace-sum average governs the variance of sums of $Λ^{*k}$ over monic polynomials in $\mathbb F_q[T]$; we denote its leading coefficient by $δ_k(c)$, where the total trace degree and matrix size grow with a fixed ratio $c$. Under a weaker shifted moments conjecture and RH, we recover this $δ_k(c)$ as the leading coefficient of the variance of short-interval sums of $Λ^{*k}$ over the integers. It is the counterpart of $γ_k(c)$, the piecewise polynomial from the variance of divisor sums, with the Dirichlet coefficients of $ζ(s)^k$ replaced by those of $\bigl(-ζ'/ζ\bigr)^k$.

title: Interpolating between 4d $\mathcal{N}= 1$ SCFT supercurrent multiplet anomalies
summary: A renormalized SCFT can be coupled to a number of background off-shell supergravity multiplets, defining different current multiplets and superconformal anomalies. We focus on the relation between the conformal and Ferrara-Zumino multiplets of generic $\mathcal{N}= 1$ SCFTs in four dimensions, defined respectively by $\mathcal{N}= 1$ conformal and old-minimal supergravity. We show that the conformal super-gravity partition function, when lifted to a functional of the old-minimal background fields through a suitable Wess-Zumino action, is related to the old-minimal partition function by a local counterterm that we determine explicitly in components. This counterterm interpolates between two different old-minimal supergravity schemes with different superconformal anomalies. Part of the counterterm depends on the old-minimal auxiliary scalar and provides the explicit component form of the super-space counterterm constructed in [1].
